To resolve this, the IT Support team performed the following steps: 1) Accessed the CRM system's configuration management interface and navigated to the 'Session Timeout Settings' under the 'Authentication Service' section. 2) Adjusted the session timeout value from 5 minutes to 30 minutes using the configuration tool. 3) Verified the change by initiating a test session with the Sales Agent's credentials and monitoring the session duration using the CRM's internal logging system. 4) Ensured that the session persistence was maintained by checking the server-side session store (Redis) to confirm that session data was not being prematurely invalidated. 5) Instructed the Sales Agent to clear their browser cache and cookies to eliminate any stale session data that might interfere with the login process. 6) Monitored the system post-implementation to ensure that no further session timeouts occurred. The issue was resolved successfully, allowing the Sales Agent to complete the onboarding process without interruption.

short_description: PDF not loading for merchant agreement review
description: Sales Agent using a legacy browser experienced a freeze while configuring equipment, leading to incomplete data entry; Sales Agent affected.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that involved multiple stages of diagnostics and remediation. The initial step was to isolate the issue by reproducing the problem in a controlled environment. The Sales Agent reported that the PDF loading issue occurred when using a legacy browser, specifically Internet Explorer 11, which is no longer supported by the application's backend services. The first diagnostic action was to check the browser compatibility matrix to confirm that the application's frontend was not designed to support IE11. This was verified by reviewing the application's supported browsers list, which indicated that only Chrome, Firefox, and Edge were supported. The next step was to inspect the session management and authentication logs to determine if there was an issue with the user's session or authentication token. The logs revealed that the user's session was being invalidated prematurely due to a mismatch in the browser's user agent string, which caused the application to redirect the user to a login page instead of allowing them to access the agreement. To resolve this, the IT team updated the UI application to include a user agent detection mechanism that would redirect users to a compatible browser if they attempted to access the application with an unsupported browser. Additionally, the team implemented a browser compatibility check during the login process, which would prompt the user to update their browser or switch to a supported one. The team also ensured that the authentication service was configured to accept cookies from the legacy browser, which was previously blocked due to security policies. This was done by modifying the CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) headers in the authentication service to allow cookies from IE11. The final step was to test the solution by having the Sales Agent re-attempt the process using a supported browser, which resulted in the PDF loading correctly without any freeze or blank screen. The incident was fully resolved, and the user was able to complete the data entry without any further issues.

short_description: Merchant UI not responsive for e-signature
description: Sales Agent encountered an error while configuring POS terminals for a merchant, leading to incorrect settings. Merchant transactions are impacted.
resolution: The incident was resolved by identifying and fixing a critical bug in the Equipment Selection Module within the Merchant Configuration Service. The Sales Agent reported that while configuring POS terminals for a merchant, the UI became unresponsive when attempting to set up e-signature functionality. Initial diagnostics involved checking the application logs, which revealed a null pointer exception in the EquipmentSelectionService.java file at line 127. This occurred when the system attempted to process a null value for the 'equipmentId' parameter during the e-signature configuration flow. The development team performed a root cause analysis using the Application Performance Management (APM) tool Datadog, which showed a spike in error rates during the e-signature setup phase. The fix involved adding a null check and a default fallback value for the 'equipmentId' parameter in the EquipmentSelectionService class. Additionally, the team implemented a validation layer to ensure all required parameters are present before invoking the e-signature configuration API. The Sales Agent was then able to reselect the equipment for the new location, and the UI responsiveness was restored. Post-resolution, the team also added automated unit tests to the CI/CD pipeline to catch similar issues in the future.

short_description: Inability to submit Merchant Agreement for e-signature
description: Sales Agent reported that the system did not recognize the merchant ID when trying to onboard an additional location. This led to a mismatch in data and prevented the new location from being linked to the correct merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that involved multiple diagnostic and remediation steps. Initially, the Sales Agent's access to the merchant data was verified by checking the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the CRM system. The RBAC settings were reviewed using the 'get-roles' API endpoint, which confirmed that the Sales Agent's role lacked the necessary permissions to view and modify merchant-specific data. To address this, the 'Merchant Management' role was assigned to the Sales Agent, granting access to the relevant data fields and APIs. Next, the system cache was cleared using the 'clear-cache' command in the CRM's administrative console, which ensured that the new location's merchant ID was properly reflected in the system. Additionally, the database was checked for any inconsistencies using the 'SELECT * FROM merchant_locations WHERE merchant_id = X' query, which revealed that the new location's entry was not correctly linked to the merchant ID. This was resolved by updating the database record using the 'UPDATE merchant_locations SET merchant_id = X WHERE location_id = Y' statement. Finally, the system's authentication service was validated to ensure that the Sales Agent's session was not expired or corrupted, which could have caused the data mismatch. The authentication logs were reviewed using the 'audit-log' tool, which confirmed that the session was active and properly authenticated. These steps collectively ensured that the Sales Agent could submit the Merchant Agreement for e-signature without any data mismatches.

short_description: Error in calculating processing fees for a merchant
description: A Sales Agent reported being unable to access the merchant equipment selection options within the Sales UI, hindering the configuration of new merchant accounts.
resolution: The incident was resolved by conducting a comprehensive diagnostic analysis of the Sales UI access permissions and the associated role-based access control (RBAC) configuration. Initial troubleshooting steps included verifying the Sales Agent's role permissions against the predefined access control policies in the Identity and Access Management (IAM) system. Using the IAM audit logs, we identified that the Sales Agent's role lacked the necessary permissions to access the merchant equipment selection options within the Sales UI. To resolve this, we executed the following steps: 1) Reassigned the 'Merchant Equipment Access' permission to the Sales Agent role in the IAM system. 2) Verified the permission changes by using the IAM access review tool, which confirmed the updated permissions. 3) Reauthenticated the Sales Agent's session to ensure the new permissions were applied. 4) Conducted a post-implementation validation by having the Sales Agent attempt to access the merchant equipment selection options again, which was successful. Additionally, we reviewed the Sales UI application logs to ensure there were no related errors or access denials, which were found to be resolved. The resolution ensured seamless fee configuration and restored full functionality for the Sales Agent.

short_description: Access Rights Restriction
description: When a merchant attempts to e-sign the agreement in the Customer UI, the interface becomes unresponsive, preventing completion of the signing process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the access rights restriction that caused the Customer UI to become unresponsive during the e-signing process. The initial step involved verifying the user's session state using browser developer tools to inspect network requests and identify any failed API calls related to the e-signature workflow. Using the Chrome DevTools, we observed that the Sales Agent's account was being blocked by the Authentication Service due to insufficient permissions on the /api/v1/e-signature endpoint. The error logs from the Authentication Service indicated a 403 Forbidden response when attempting to access the e-signature resource, confirming the access rights issue. We then reviewed the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the Identity and Access Management (IAM) system, which showed that the Sales Agent role lacked the necessary permissions for the e-signature module. To resolve this, we updated the IAM policy to grant the Sales Agent role the 'e-signature:execute' permission, ensuring the account could interact with the e-signature service without interruption. Additionally, we validated the configuration using the IAM CLI tool, which confirmed the updated permissions were applied successfully. Finally, we performed a regression test by simulating the e-signing process with the Sales Agent account, which completed without errors, confirming the fix. The resolution also included a recommendation to implement automated monitoring for RBAC changes to prevent similar issues in the future.

short_description: Merchant UI not responsive for e-signature
description: Merchants report that the content of the Merchant Agreement PDF appears distorted and unreadable when accessed for review and e-signature.
resolution:
The issue with the Merchant UI not being responsive for e-signature was resolved through a systematic analysis and targeted correction of the underlying configuration and access controls. The initial investigation revealed that merchants were encountering distorted PDF content when attempting to review and e-signature the Merchant Agreement, which was traced back to a misconfigured access control policy for the Sales Agent role. This misconfiguration was preventing proper rendering of the PDF content, leading to the observed distortion. To resolve this, the following steps were taken: 

1. **Access Control Review**: The access permissions for the Sales Agent role were thoroughly reviewed using the Identity and Access Management (IAM) console. This involved checking the role's policy document to ensure it included the necessary permissions for accessing the fee configuration page. The policy was updated to explicitly grant access to the relevant API endpoints and UI components, ensuring that Sales Agents could interact with the fee configuration without restrictions.

2. **Permission Testing**: After updating the policy, a series of tests were conducted to verify the changes. This included logging in as a Sales Agent and attempting to access the fee configuration page. The tests confirmed that the updated permissions allowed seamless configuration of fees for merchant accounts without any access issues.

3. **Application and Infrastructure Validation**: The application's infrastructure was validated to ensure that the updated permissions were correctly propagated. This involved checking the deployment pipelines and ensuring that the updated IAM policies were applied to the relevant environments. Additionally, the application logs were reviewed for any errors related to access denied or permission issues, which were found to be resolved after the policy update.

4. **User Communication and Rollout**: Once the permissions were corrected, the changes were rolled out to all affected environments. Users were notified of the resolution and advised to log out and back in to ensure the new permissions took effect. Post-implementation, a follow-up was conducted to confirm that the issue was fully resolved and that no further access issues were encountered.

These steps ensured that the Sales Agent role had the necessary permissions to access and configure the fee settings, thereby resolving the issue with the Merchant UI responsiveness for e-signature.

short_description: Error message 'Invalid Signature' when attempting to e-sign Agreement
description: Sales Agent faced intermittent network disconnections during equipment selection, causing data loss and frustration; Sales Agent affected.
resolution: The incident was resolved by identifying and addressing a backend synchronization issue between the CRM system and the e-signature service. The root cause was traced to a misconfigured API key in the e-signature service's authentication layer, which led to invalid signature errors when attempting to e-sign agreements. The following diagnostic steps were performed: 1. Checked the e-signature service logs for error patterns, revealing frequent 'Invalid Signature' errors during API requests. 2. Performed a packet capture using Wireshark to analyze network traffic between the CRM and e-signature service, confirming that the API requests were being rejected due to authentication failures. 3. Reviewed the API key configuration in the e-signature service's authentication service, which was found to be using an expired key. 4. Replaced the expired API key with a new one generated through the e-signature service's key management system. 5. Verified the resolution by initiating a manual sync process between the CRM and e-signature service, which successfully re-established the required authentication and data synchronization. The Sales Agent confirmed that the fees and services configurations were now accurately displayed, and the e-signature process was functioning without errors.

short_description: API endpoint returning 500 error for merchant creation
description: A merchant encounters an error when trying to electronically sign the Merchant Agreement in the Customer UI.
resolution: The incident, tracked under INC00320, involved a critical failure in the API endpoint responsible for merchant creation, resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error during the electronic signature process of the Merchant Agreement. The root cause was identified as a synchronization discrepancy between the Sales UI and the agreement generation module. Initial diagnostic steps included reviewing server logs, specifically focusing on the API gateway logs for the /api/v1/merchants/create endpoint. These logs revealed a 500 error with the message 'Internal Server Error: Failed to serialize agreement data'. Further investigation uncovered that the Sales UI was not correctly transmitting the configured fees and services to the agreement generation module, leading to a deserialization failure in the backend service. To resolve this, we executed a data synchronization script that enforced a bidirectional check between the Sales UI and the agreement module. Additionally, a patch was applied to the agreement generation service to enhance data validation and ensure that all required fields, including fees and services, were correctly populated. The patch included a fix for a known issue in the JSON serialization library, which was causing malformed payloads under certain conditions. The resolution was verified by re-running the end-to-end test scenario, which confirmed that the agreement was successfully generated and signed without errors. The incident was escalated to the development team for a permanent fix, and a permanent patch was deployed during the next scheduled maintenance window.

short_description: Error message 'Invalid Signature' when attempting to e-sign Agreement
description: When a merchant attempts to e-sign the agreement in the Customer UI, the interface becomes unresponsive, preventing completion of the signing process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. Initial troubleshooting began with capturing user session logs and analyzing the e-signature workflow. The error 'Invalid Signature' was traced to a misconfiguration in the Authentication Service's token validation logic. The team used the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) to filter and analyze logs from the Customer UI and backend API calls. The root cause was identified as a mismatch between the JWT token's signature algorithm (HS256) and the server's expected algorithm (RS256) during the e-signature verification phase. To resolve this, the development team updated the token validation middleware in the Authentication Service to enforce HS256 for all e-signature-related tokens. Additionally, the team implemented a rollback plan for the token validation logic to ensure compatibility with existing systems. A regression test suite was executed using Postman and JMeter to validate the fix, and all e-signature workflows were manually tested with a subset of merchants. Finally, the fix was deployed via a blue-green deployment strategy to minimize downtime and ensure a smooth rollback if needed.

short_description: Merchant unable to e-sign agreement
description: An issue was detected where the fee configuration tool within the Sales UI was malfunctioning, leading to incorrect fee structures being applied to merchant accounts, impacting financial agreements.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. First, the IT Support team identified that the issue stemmed from the fee configuration tool within the Sales UI, which was erroneously applying incorrect fee structures to merchant accounts. Initial troubleshooting involved verifying the merchant's access credentials and ensuring proper authentication through the Authentication Service. However, the root cause was traced to a misconfiguration in the fee calculation module of the Sales UI, which was incorrectly processing the fee parameters. To resolve this, the team executed the following steps: 1. Checked the Sales UI's backend logs for any errors or exceptions, focusing on the fee calculation endpoint (/api/sales/fee-calculation). 2. Performed a database query to validate the fee structure data stored in the merchant's account, using SQL commands like SELECT * FROM fee_structures WHERE merchant_id = 'M12345'; 3. Reinitialized the Sales UI's fee calculation module by restarting the associated microservice using systemctl restart sales-ui-fee-calc. 4. Validated the correction by reapplying the fee structure through the UI and confirming the correct charges were calculated. Additionally, the team implemented a temporary workaround by granting the merchant access to a staging environment to review and e-sign the agreement while the permanent fix was being developed. The permanent fix involved updating the fee configuration tool's logic to ensure accurate fee application, which was deployed via a patch release. The incident was escalated to the development team for a deeper code review and to prevent recurrence.

short_description: Unable to add new location due to POS terminal malfunction
description: During equipment selection for a new merchant, Sales Agents are experiencing an issue where the dropdown menu for selecting equipment models is not loading, causing delays in onboarding.
resolution: The issue was diagnosed as a misconfiguration in the Payment Gateway integration with the POS terminal, which caused the equipment model dropdown menu to fail loading during merchant onboarding. Initial troubleshooting involved checking the terminal's firmware version and confirming compatibility with the current POS system software. The IT Support team executed a series of diagnostic commands, including `telnet <gateway_ip> 80` to verify connectivity, and reviewed the gateway's access logs for any 403 or 503 errors. The terminal's integration with the Payment Gateway was found to be blocked due to an outdated API version, which was causing the dropdown menu to hang during data retrieval. To resolve this, the team updated the Payment Gateway's API version to v3.2.1, reconfigured the terminal's backend settings using the `configure_terminal --api_version 3.2.1` command, and validated the changes by simulating a merchant onboarding process. Additionally, the team ensured that the terminal's TLS certificate was up to date and that the firewall rules allowed traffic on port 443. After these changes, the equipment model dropdown menu functioned correctly, and the Sales Agents were able to proceed with onboarding without further delays.

short_description: Unable to select specific POS terminal model
description: During the data upload process for a new merchant, the API endpoint consistently returns a 500 error, preventing sales agents from successfully onboarding the merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and configuration process. Initial logs indicated a 500 Internal Server Error when attempting to communicate with the POS terminal model during the merchant onboarding workflow. The team first validated the API endpoint health by using curl -v https://api.paymentgateway.com/v1/terminals to check for connectivity. The response showed a 500 error with the server log entry: "Error 500: Terminal model 'POS-2000' not found in configuration database (DBID: 12345)." This pointed to a misconfiguration in the payment terminal database. The IT Support team then executed a database query to inspect the terminal models: SELECT * FROM terminal_models WHERE model_id = 'POS-2000'; The query returned no results, confirming the model was not registered. The team then used the terminal management CLI tool (tmcli) to import the missing model: tmcli import-model --file=POS-2000.json. After importing, a verification script was run: tmcli verify-model --model-id=POS-2000, which confirmed successful registration. Finally, the API endpoint was retested with a POST request containing the terminal model details, resulting in a 201 Created response. This resolved the issue, allowing sales agents to onboard merchants without encountering the 50,000 error.

short_description: Unable to link new location to existing merchant ID
description: Merchants report that the content of the Merchant Agreement PDF appears distorted and unreadable when accessed for review and e-signature.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. Initial investigation revealed that the PDF distortion issue was caused by a misconfiguration in the document rendering pipeline, specifically within the Sales UI component. The following steps were taken: 1. Performed a system cache refresh using the 'clear_cache.sh' script, which purges temporary files and reloads merchant data from the database. 2. Verified data mapping integrity by querying the 'merchant_data' table with the command 'SELECT * FROM merchant_data WHERE merchant_id = 'M12345';' to ensure proper field alignment. 3. Inspected the PDF generation process by reviewing logs from the 'pdf_renderer' service, which indicated a version mismatch between the PDF library (version 2.1.3) and the expected library (version 2.2.1). 4. Updated the PDF library using 'npm install pdf-lib@2.2.1' to align with the required version. 5. Conducted a full system reload with 'system_reload.sh' to ensure all components were synchronized. 6. Validated the fix by re-accessing the Sales UI and confirming that the PDF content was now displayed correctly without distortion. Additionally, a temporary workaround was implemented to prevent similar issues in the future by configuring the 'pdf_renderer' service to automatically refresh its library version during scheduled maintenance windows.

short_description: Unable to select equipment for merchant
description: During the onboarding process for an additional location, the Sales Agent received an error message stating 'Location already exists' even though it's a new location being added. This issue caused confusion and delays in completing the merchant setup.
resolution: The incident was caused by a duplicate location entry in the database, which led to the 'Location already exists' error when attempting to onboard a new merchant. To resolve this, the following steps were taken: 1. Database query analysis: The team executed a SELECT query on the 'locations' table to identify duplicate entries. The query was: SELECT * FROM locations WHERE location_name = 'New Location'; This revealed two entries with identical names. 2. Data deduplication: A DELETE statement was used to remove the duplicate entry: DELETE FROM locations WHERE location_id = '12345'; 3. Index optimization: An index was added to the 'location_name' column to improve query performance: ALTER TABLE locations ADD INDEX idx_location_name (location_name); 4. Application-level validation: A check was implemented in the onboarding workflow to ensure location names are unique before allowing submission. This was done by adding a unique constraint to the 'location_name' field in the database schema. 5. Monitoring enhancement: A new alert was configured in the monitoring system to notify the team when duplicate entries are detected. The resolution ensured that the onboarding process could proceed without errors, and the merchant setup was completed successfully.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access merchant equipment options
description: While configuring equipment for a new merchant, Sales Agent experienced network timeouts leading to delays in selecting the required hardware, affecting the efficiency of onboarding processes.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic troubleshooting process that began with verifying the Sales Agent's access credentials and session integrity. First, the IT Support team confirmed that the Sales Agent's login credentials were valid by checking the authentication logs in the onboarding portal's database. The logs indicated no unauthorized access attempts, so the issue was likely related to session expiration or token invalidation. Next, the team executed a session reset by clearing the Sales Agent's browser cookies and local storage, which is a common cause of authentication issues. They then used the 'curl' command to test the portal's authentication endpoint, which returned a 401 Unauthorized error, confirming the session was invalid. To resolve this, the IT team performed a forced logout by sending a POST request to the /api/logout endpoint, which invalidated the current session. Following this, the Sales Agent was redirected to the login page, where they were able to re-authenticate successfully. Additionally, the team checked the network latency between the Sales Agent's location and the onboarding portal's server using the 'ping' and 'traceroute' commands, which revealed a minor delay of 150ms. This delay was attributed to a temporary routing issue in the Network Infrastructure. The team then implemented a temporary workaround by adjusting the DNS settings to prioritize a more stable route. Finally, the Sales Agent was able to access the merchant equipment options without further interruptions, and the onboarding process resumed normally.

short_description: Critical Service Fee Configuration Failure
description: Sales Agent encountered a system error indicating a duplicate Merchant ID while setting up a new location, leading to confusion and inability to proceed with onboarding.
resolution: Upon initial investigation, the Sales Agent encountered a 'Duplicate Merchant ID' error while attempting to onboard a new location. The error indicated that the merchant ID already existed in the system, but the agent was unaware of its prior registration. The root cause was identified as a misconfiguration in the authentication service, where the system failed to validate the uniqueness of the merchant ID during the onboarding process. To resolve this, the following steps were executed: 1. The authentication service logs were reviewed using the command `tail -f /var/log/auth-service.log` to trace the exact moment the duplicate ID was detected. 2. A database query was executed to check for existing entries in the merchant database: `SELECT * FROM merchants WHERE merchant_id = 'M12345';` This confirmed the presence of the duplicate ID. 3. The affected merchant's configuration was corrected by updating the merchant_id in the database to a unique value using the SQL command `UPDATE merchants SET merchant_id = 'M12345A' WHERE merchant_id = 'M12345';`. 4. The authentication service was then restarted to apply the changes: `sudo systemctl restart auth-service`. 5. The Sales Agent's access credentials were reset to ensure a clean session, and they were instructed to re-initiate the onboarding process. The resolution ensured that the onboarding process could proceed without further interruptions, and the system was validated by retesting the merchant ID creation process.

short_description: Payment terminal integration failure during merchant setup
description: While submitting location data for a merchant ID, a sudden network outage occurred, interrupting the data transmission process. This outage impacted the Sales Agent's ability to finalize the onboarding for the merchant, causing delays and data loss.
resolution: The incident was traced to a network outage that occurred during the transmission of location data for merchant onboarding, which disrupted the Payment Gateway integration process. The root cause was identified as a transient network latency issue between the merchant's onboarding server and the Payment Gateway API endpoint. To resolve the issue, the following steps were executed: 1) Network diagnostics were performed using the `traceroute` and `mtr` commands to analyze latency and packet loss between the merchant's server and the Payment Gateway's API endpoint. 2) The `tcpdump` tool was used to capture and analyze network traffic, revealing intermittent packet loss and reordering. 3) The `ping` command was utilized to measure latency, showing a spike in round-trip time (RTT) during the data submission phase. 4) The Payment Gateway's API endpoint was tested using `curl` with verbose output, which confirmed that the request was being received but the response was not being properly acknowledged due to a misconfigured firewall rule on the server. 5) The firewall rules were updated to allow traffic on the required port (e.g., port 443 for HTTPS) and to prioritize traffic from the merchant's onboarding server. 6) A temporary workaround was implemented by redirecting the request through a redundant network path using a load balancer, which improved reliability during the resolution process. 7) The Payment Gateway integration was retested using automated smoke tests and integration tests to ensure that the data transmission process was stable and reliable. The fix involved ensuring that the network infrastructure could handle the required throughput and that the firewall rules were configured to allow uninterrupted communication between the onboarding server and the Payment Gateway API. Additionally, a monitoring alert was set up using Prometheus and Grafana to track network latency and packet loss in real-time, preventing similar incidents in the future.

short_description: Intermittent connection issues while configuring services
description: Sales Agent reported that when configuring bundled services for a merchant, the system was incorrectly calculating the total fees, leading to discrepancies in the final pricing.
resolution: Upon receiving the incident report, the IT Support team initiated a detailed investigation into the intermittent connection issues affecting the configuration of bundled services. The first step was to isolate the issue by checking the network connectivity between the Sales Agent's workstation and the backend configuration server. Using the ping command with the -c option to send 100 packets, we observed packet loss and increased latency, indicating a possible network congestion or misconfiguration. The next diagnostic step involved checking the router configuration using the show running-config command on the Cisco IOS router. This revealed an incorrect QoS policy that was prioritizing non-critical traffic over the configuration service traffic, leading to intermittent connectivity. To resolve this, the QoS policy was adjusted to ensure that the configuration service traffic was prioritized with a higher DSCP value. Additionally, the team performed a traceroute from the Sales Agent's workstation to the configuration server to identify any potential bottlenecks or routing anomalies. The traceroute output showed that the traffic was being rerouted through an overloaded intermediate router, which was then configured to use a more direct path. The team also reviewed the system logs on the configuration server using the tail -f /var/log/syslog command, which showed intermittent connection resets and timeouts, confirming the network-related nature of the issue. Finally, the network infrastructure was thoroughly tested with the iperf tool to measure throughput and ensure stable connectivity. The resolution was confirmed by retesting the configuration process, which now completed without any connectivity issues or fee calculation discrepancies.

short_description: PDF agreement not loading for Merchant
description: Sales Agent encountered a system error indicating a duplicate Merchant ID while setting up a new location, leading to confusion and inability to proceed with onboarding.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. The resolution also included clearing the Sales Agent's browser cache and cookies to eliminate any potential session conflicts. short_description: Incorrect fees applied for services
description: A critical failure in configuring service fees by a Sales Agent has caused all merchant accounts to reflect incorrect service charges. Financial discrepancies detected.
resolution: Upon investigation, the root cause of the issue was identified as a misconfiguration in the service fee calculation logic within the Payment Gateway component. The Sales Agent had manually adjusted the fee percentages without updating the backend configuration, resulting in inconsistent fee application across all merchant accounts. To resolve this, the following steps were executed: 1. Diagnosed the issue by querying the database to identify affected accounts using SQL command: SELECT * FROM merchant_accounts WHERE fee_percentage != 15.0; 2. Reviewed the Payment Gateway logs (accessed via /var/log/payment_gateway.log) to trace the incorrect fee application. 3. Implemented a software patch to correct the fee calculation algorithm, ensuring accurate fee configurations for all new and existing merchant accounts. 4. Validated the fix by running automated tests and verifying the fee calculations against a sample dataset. 5. Notified affected merchants via the CRM system to inform them of the correction and provide guidance on reconciling their accounts. 6. Scheduled a review of the configuration management process to prevent similar incidents in the future.

short_description: Touchscreen malfunction on Merchant's device for e-signing
description: A Sales Agent reported being unable to access the fee configuration module in the application, hindering their ability to customize services for a new merchant.
resolution: The incident was initiated when a Sales Agent reported an inability to access the fee configuration module in the application, which is critical for customizing services for a new merchant. The initial troubleshooting steps included verifying the Sales Agent's access rights and ensuring the application's availability through the IT Support team. The IT Support team performed a systematic diagnostic process, starting with checking the network connectivity of the Sales Agent's device using the 'ping' and 'tracert' commands to ensure there were no network-related issues. They then validated the device's touchscreen functionality by running a series of diagnostic tests using the built-in Windows Device Manager and the 'dxdiag' tool to check for hardware-related errors. The diagnostic results indicated a hardware fault in the touchscreen component, specifically a short circuit in the digitizer layer. The Sales Agent was then able to access the fee configuration module and complete the necessary tasks without further impediments. The incident was resolved successfully, and no further actions were required.

short_description: Access permission error for Merchant Agreement PDF upload
description: Merchants are unable to view the PDF Merchant Agreement after logging in to the Customer UI.
resolution: The incident was resolved by conducting a comprehensive investigation into the access permission error for the Merchant Agreement PDF upload. Initial diagnostic steps included reviewing server-side access control lists (ACLs) using the 'getfacl' command on the Linux-based file server hosting the PDF files. The audit logs from the application server were analyzed using the 'tail -f /var/log/apache2/access.log' command to identify any access denial patterns. It was discovered that the file permissions were incorrectly set to '644' instead of '664', restricting access to the merchant user groups. Additionally, the web application's configuration file, 'config.php', was checked for any misconfigured access control settings. The 'chmod 664' command was executed to adjust the file permissions, allowing read and write access for the merchant user group. Furthermore, the application's access control module was reviewed to ensure that the merchant roles were properly mapped to the required file access rights. The 'audit.log' was also examined to confirm that the changes were effective, and no further access denials were observed. Finally, a test user account was created with the same permissions as the affected merchants to validate the resolution through a simulated upload and view operation.

short_description: Equipment Selection Error for High-Volume Merchant
description: Merchant unable to locate the e-signature field within the Merchant Agreement PDF for completing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach to diagnose and correct the access issue affecting the Sales Agent role. The initial step involved verifying the access permissions for the Sales Agent role within the CRM system. This was done by querying the access control list (ACL) using the command `aclctl --list --role SalesAgent`. The output indicated that the Sales Agent role was missing the necessary permissions to access the fee configuration page. To address this, the permissions were updated by running the command `aclctl --grant --role SalesAgent --resource fee-configuration-page --action read-write`. Additionally, the system logs were reviewed for any authentication errors related to the Sales Agent role, which revealed a pattern of 403 Forbidden errors when attempting to access the fee configuration page. These logs were cross-referenced with the user's session data to identify any session-related issues. The session data was checked using the `sessionctl --list --user <username>` command, which showed that the session was not properly initialized for the Sales Agent role. To resolve this, the session initialization process was modified to ensure that the Sales Agent role's session is properly configured upon login. The changes were implemented and tested in a staging environment before being rolled out to production. The final step involved verifying the resolution by having the affected merchant test the onboarding process, which confirmed that the e-signature field was now accessible and the onboarding process was completed successfully.

short_description: Error accessing merchant agreement PDF
description: Sales Agent encountered an issue where a specific POS terminal model, 'ABC-2000', could not be selected while configuring equipment for a merchant.
resolution: The issue with Error accessing merchant agreement PDF was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and resolution process. The Sales Agent reported that the POS terminal model 'ABC-2000' could not be selected while configuring equipment for a merchant, which resulted in an error when attempting to access the merchant agreement PDF. The root cause was identified as a browser-specific caching issue affecting the Customer UI. The resolution involved the following steps: 1. The affected browser was cleared of its cache using the 'Clear browsing data' function in Chrome, ensuring all temporary internet files, cookies, and cached images were removed. 2. The browser's cookies were deleted manually through the 'Cookies' section in the browser settings to eliminate any session-specific data that might have been causing the error. 3. The Customer UI was reloaded to ensure that the latest version of the application was loaded without any cached data. 4. The Sales Agent was instructed to log out of the system and log back in to clear any session-related authentication tokens. 5. The system logs were reviewed to confirm that there were no backend errors, and the PDF file was successfully generated and accessible. The resolution was verified by the Sales Agent, who was able to select the 'ABC-2000' model and access the PDF without any issues.

short_description: Intermittent connection issues while configuring services
description: Sales Agent encountered an issue where merchant data input was not saving correctly in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete merchant profiles and delays in onboarding.
resolution: The intermittent connection issues experienced by the Sales Agent were traced to a compatibility problem between the legacy POS system (Model XYZ-7000) and the Sales UI application. Initial diagnostics involved capturing network traffic using Wireshark to identify packet loss and latency during data submission. The Sales UI logs revealed HTTP 500 errors when attempting to POST merchant data, indicating a backend processing failure. Further investigation into the Sales UI application logs showed that the POS model was not recognized by the system's device compatibility module, which was causing the data to be rejected at the API layer. To resolve this, the system's device compatibility module was updated with the latest firmware for the XYZ-7000 POS model. Additionally, the Sales UI was patched to include a new device identifier in its request payload. The fix was validated by simulating the POS model's communication protocol using tcpdump and verifying that the POST requests were successfully processed by the backend service. Post-resolution, a regression test was conducted to ensure that no other POS models were affected by the update. The issue was fully resolved after deploying the patch to the production environment and confirming successful data submission through the Sales UI.

short_description: Error saving merchant data in Sales UI
description: When trying to select equipment for a newly added location, the dropdown menu is not populating with the available options, hindering the configuration process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the permission misconfiguration that was preventing the submission button from functioning in the Sales UI. The initial step involved verifying the user's access rights by checking the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the Identity and Access Management (IAM) system. This was done using the IAM API to query the user's permissions, which revealed that the Sales Agent's role lacked the necessary 'equipment_selection' permission. To validate this, we executed the following commands: `curl -X GET https://iam-api.example.com/v1/users/12345/permissions` and reviewed the response, which confirmed the missing permission. Next, the system administrator updated the role definition in the IAM system to include the 'equipment_selection' permission, ensuring that the Sales Agents could interact with the dropdown menu for equipment selection. Additionally, we performed a cache invalidation on the frontend application to ensure that the updated permissions were reflected immediately. The resolution also included a review of the application logs to confirm that the submission button was no longer restricted, using the command `tail -f /var/log/app.log` to monitor real-time log entries. Finally, a regression test was conducted to ensure that the fix did not introduce any new issues, and the Sales UI was validated by simulating the equipment selection process for a newly added location.

short_description: Error message 'Invalid Signature' when attempting to e-sign Agreement
description: Sales Agent reports that configured fees and services for a new merchant are not saving upon submission, leading to incorrect pricing in the agreement.
resolution: The incident was caused by a backend synchronization issue between the CRM system and the e-signature service, which resulted in the 'Invalid Signature' error when attempting to e-sign an agreement. The root cause was identified through the following steps: 1. Checked the CRM system logs for any errors or warnings around the time of the incident, which showed failed synchronization attempts with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. 2. Performed a detailed analysis of the e-signature service logs, which revealed that the signature validation process was failing due to a mismatch between the expected and actual signature hashes. 3. Verified the integrity of the data being sent from the CRM to the e-signature service by running a data consistency check using the CRM's API endpoint /api/v1/sync/validate. This check confirmed that the data payloads contained invalid or corrupted signature fields. 4. Investigated the database schema for the CRM and e-signature service to ensure that the signature fields were properly indexed and stored as expected. 5. Reverted to a known good state by restoring the CRM database from a backup taken before the synchronization issue occurred. 6. Manually triggered a synchronization process using the CRM's synchronization tool, which successfully reconciled the data and resolved the 'Invalid Signature' error. The Sales Agent confirmed that the fees and services configurations were now accurately displayed, and the e-signature process was functioning correctly.

short_description: Unable to add new location for merchant ID 12345
description: Sales Agents noticed that the service fees configured for a merchant were not displaying accurately on the summary page, potentially causing confusion during the final review with the merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved by thoroughly investigating the root cause of the inaccurate service fee display for merchant ID 12345. Initial diagnostics involved checking the Sales Agent's device for browser-specific issues, including clearing browser cache and cookies, and verifying that the latest version of the web application was installed. However, these steps did not resolve the issue. Further analysis revealed that the problem was not related to the device but rather to the backend system processing merchant data. The affected component was the CRM system, specifically the module responsible for rendering the merchant summary page. The team executed a series of diagnostic commands, including querying the database for merchant ID 12345's service fee records using SQL commands such as SELECT * FROM merchant_service_fees WHERE merchant_id = '12345';. The query returned inconsistent results, indicating a possible data corruption or synchronization issue. The team then checked the application logs for any errors related to merchant data retrieval, which showed a recurring 'Invalid data format' error when processing the specific merchant's fees. To address this, the CRM system was temporarily scaled down, and the affected module was redeployed with the latest patch. Additionally, the service fees were manually recalculated and updated in the database to ensure accuracy. Once the redeployment was complete, the Sales Agent was instructed to refresh the summary page, which now correctly displayed the service fees. The issue was confirmed to be resolved after a series of validation tests were performed, including re-checking the data in the database and verifying the frontend display against the backend records.

short_description: Critical Service Fee Configuration Failure
description: Merchants intermittently experienced data loss while reviewing the merchant agreement, leading to frustration and delays in the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and resolution process. Initial troubleshooting indicated that the issue stemmed from a misconfiguration in the Service Fee Calculation Engine, which was causing intermittent data loss when merchants reviewed their agreements. The first step involved analyzing the browser console logs using Chrome DevTools to identify any network errors or failed requests. We discovered that the Service Fee Calculation Engine was returning 500 Internal Server Errors when attempting to load the PDF agreement. Further investigation using the browser's Network tab revealed that the request to the /api/v1/agreements/{merchantId}/pdf endpoint was failing with a 500 error, despite the backend service being operational. To isolate the issue, we performed a deep dive into the backend logs using the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) and found that the Service Fee Calculation Engine was encountering a null pointer exception when processing certain merchant data. This was traced back to an incomplete or corrupted configuration in the Service Fee Calculation Engine's database schema, which was not properly initializing the required parameters for the PDF generation process. To resolve this, we executed a database schema validation script using the Liquibase tool, which ensured that all required tables and columns were correctly populated. Additionally, we implemented a configuration refresh script that periodically checks and updates the Service Fee Calculation Engine's configuration to prevent similar issues in the future. As a temporary mitigation, we also instructed affected users to clear their browser cache and cookies, which resolved the issue for them by forcing a reload of the Customer UI and ensuring that the latest configuration was fetched from the server. The resolution involved a combination of frontend and backend diagnostics, configuration validation, and proactive script implementation to ensure long-term stability.

short_description: Merchant data not transitioning to PROCESSING stage after e-signing
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to add a new POS system for a high-volume merchant, leading to delays in onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic process that began with verifying the Sales Agent's device connectivity and ensuring all system dependencies were operational. Initially, the Sales Agent's workstation was checked for network stability using the 'ping' command to confirm DNS resolution and latency. Subsequently, the system logs were reviewed using the 'journalctl -u pos-service' command, which revealed a recurring error related to the POS system integration module failing to transition merchant data to the PROCESSING stage. The error log indicated a timeout exception in the e-signature service, specifically at line 457 of the 'esignature_handler.py' file. Further investigation using the 'strace' command confirmed that the service was unable to establish a connection to the backend processing API endpoint due to a misconfigured load balancer routing rule. The resolution involved updating the load balancer configuration to correctly route traffic to the designated processing service, which was verified using the 'curl -v https://api.processing.stage' command. Additionally, the Sales Agent's browser cache was cleared and cookies were reset to eliminate any potential session-related issues. Finally, the POS system was reinitialized through the 'pos-service reset' command, which successfully transitioned the merchant data to the PROCESSING stage. The entire resolution process took approximately 2 hours, with the service restored to full functionality by the end of the incident window.

short_description: Error saving merchant data in Sales UI
description: An issue arose where certain hardware configurations selected by Sales Agents were not compatible with the fee calculation module, resulting in incorrect fee estimations and potential financial discrepancies.
resolution: The incident was caused by a server-side bug in the fee calculation module, which failed to validate hardware compatibility configurations selected by Sales Agents. The bug resulted in incorrect fee estimations and potential financial discrepancies. To resolve the issue, the team implemented a fix that enhanced the validation logic in the fee calculation module. The fix included adding a hardware compatibility check during the fee calculation process, ensuring that only compatible configurations are processed. The patch was deployed using a blue-green deployment strategy to minimize downtime and ensure a smooth transition. Post-deployment, the team performed a series of automated tests to verify the fix, including unit tests, integration tests, and load tests to ensure the solution was robust and scalable. The incident was resolved successfully, and the Sales UI was restored to full functionality without any further issues.

short_description: Equipment selection dropdown missing options
description: Sales Agent encountered an issue where a specific POS terminal model, 'ABC-2000', could not be selected while configuring equipment for a merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic approach. short_description: Login credentials not working for merchant
description: The Sales UI is not loading properly for a new Sales Agent attempting to onboard a merchant, causing delays in merchant data input.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the Sales Agent's access rights within the Authentication Service, which manages user permissions for the Sales UI. The Sales Agent's role was checked using the 'get_user_permissions' API endpoint, which returned an incomplete set of permissions for merchant onboarding tasks. To resolve this, the IT Support team adjusted the Sales Agent's access rights by updating the 'merchant_onboarding' flag in the user's role configuration within the Authentication Service. Additionally, a review of the Sales UI logs revealed a temporary session token expiration issue, which was addressed by extending the session timeout duration from 15 minutes to 30 minutes in the application's configuration file. The Sales UI was then restarted to apply the changes. Finally, the onboarding process was resumed for the affected merchant, and the Sales Agent was reauthenticated to ensure the updated permissions and session settings were active. All steps were confirmed through the system's monitoring tools, ensuring the resolution was complete and the issue was fully mitigated.

short_description: Hardware failure on Sales Agent's device
description: Merchants encountering access permissions error when trying to view the Merchant Agreement PDF for e-signing, causing delays in agreement completion.
resolution: The incident was caused by a duplicate merchant ID issue in the database, which led to access permissions errors when merchants attempted to view the Merchant Agreement PDF for e-signing. To resolve this, a comprehensive diagnostic process was initiated. First, the database was queried using SQL commands such as SELECT * FROM merchants WHERE merchant_id IN (SELECT merchant_id FROM merchant_permissions GROUP BY merchant_id HAVING COUNT(merchant_id) > 1) to identify duplicate entries. The affected records were then cross-referenced with the merchant_permissions table to ensure accurate mapping of access rights. Once duplicates were confirmed, a database maintenance script was executed to normalize the merchant_id field, ensuring uniqueness across the entire dataset. Additionally, a validation check was implemented during the onboarding process using a stored procedure that enforces unique constraints on the merchant_id column. This was done by adding a UNIQUE constraint to the merchant_id column in the merchants table, which automatically prevents the insertion of duplicate IDs. To further mitigate the issue, a database index was created on the merchant_id column to optimize query performance and ensure quick validation during onboarding. The system was also monitored using database monitoring tools like Prometheus and Grafana to track any potential duplicates in real-time. Finally, a rollback plan was prepared in case the changes caused unintended side effects, ensuring business continuity during the resolution process.

short_description: Error accessing merchant agreement PDF
description: Sales Agent encountered an issue where merchant data input was not saving correctly in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete merchant profiles and delays in onboarding.
resolution: The issue with the Sales UI failing to save merchant data correctly was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and data reconciliation process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the integrity of the merchant data in the CRM system. The Sales UI was observed to be pulling data from the CRM's database, but the data was not persisting due to an underlying data synchronization problem. The team executed a database query to check the merchant records, which revealed that the data was being stored in a temporary cache rather than the main database. A data refresh was initiated using the CRM's API endpoint /api/merchant/data-refresh, which triggered a batch synchronization process. The synchronization was monitored via the CRM's logging system, which showed that the data was successfully migrated to the main database. Additionally, the Sales UI was configured to use the main database instead of the cache, ensuring that future data inputs would be saved directly. The issue was further validated by retesting the data input process, which confirmed that the merchant profiles were now being saved correctly without any delays. The root cause was identified as a misconfiguration in the Sales UI's data source settings, which was corrected to ensure proper data persistence.

short_description: Merchant ID duplication error during new location setup
description: Sales Agent noticed that any changes made to fees/services configurations for a merchant are not saving properly in the system.
resolution: The incident was resolved by thoroughly investigating the session management and authentication flow within the merchant portal. Initial diagnostics revealed that the session timeout settings were too aggressive, causing the session to expire before the configuration changes could be saved. To address this, we modified the session timeout duration in the application's configuration file (config/session_timeout.js) from 15 minutes to 30 minutes. Additionally, we implemented a persistent session token mechanism using JWT (JSON Web Tokens) to maintain state across requests without relying solely on server-side sessions. We also reviewed the backend API endpoints responsible for configuration updates (POST /api/v1/merchants/configure) and ensured they were handling token validation correctly. The issue was further validated by checking the server logs (access.log and auth.log) for any session expiration events, which showed a significant reduction in premature session terminations. Finally, we instructed merchants to clear their browser cache and cookies, and to ensure they were using a supported browser with updated TLS settings. These steps ensured that the configuration changes were saved successfully without session interruptions.

short_description: Hardware failure on Sales Agent's device
description: Intermittent latency spikes were observed, causing delays in API responses during merchant data input by Sales Agents. This variability in response times impacted the overall speed of onboarding operations.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-faceted approach targeting both the root cause and the mitigation of future occurrences. Initially, we conducted a comprehensive diagnostic analysis of the Sales Agent's device and the underlying infrastructure. We began by monitoring the system using Prometheus and Grafana to identify latency spikes in API responses. The metrics revealed that the issue was related to the CRM system's API endpoint responsible for merchant data input, which was experiencing intermittent latency due to insufficient hardware resources on the Sales Agent's device. To address this, we executed a series of diagnostic commands such as 'htop' and 'iostat' to assess CPU and disk usage, which indicated that the device was underperforming due to insufficient RAM and CPU capacity. Additionally, we analyzed the system logs using 'journalctl -u crm-api-service' and found that the service was occasionally crashing due to memory exhaustion. To resolve the issue, we upgraded the Sales Agent's device to a higher-spec model with increased RAM and CPU capacity. Furthermore, we implemented a proactive monitoring solution using Nagios to continuously track system performance metrics and ensure early detection of potential issues. To prevent future occurrences, we also introduced a load balancing mechanism using HAProxy to distribute the API load across multiple instances, reducing the risk of single points of failure. Finally, we configured automated scaling policies in Kubernetes to dynamically scale the CRM service based on real-time demand, ensuring consistent performance during peak usage periods.

short_description: Equipment selection dropdown missing options
description: Sales agents are encountering a hardware malfunction that is preventing them from selecting equipment for new merchants during the onboarding process. This issue is limiting the options available to merchants.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic approach. Initial investigation revealed that the equipment selection dropdown was not displaying options due to an incomplete API response from the Inventory Service. The Sales Agent's browser console showed a 503 Service Unavailable error when attempting to fetch equipment options. The IT Support team executed the following steps: 1. Checked the Inventory Service's health endpoint at https://inventory-api.example.com/health, which returned a 503 error. 2. Inspected the Inventory Service's logs using the command 'kubectl logs -n inventory inventory-service-pod-123' which indicated a database connection timeout. 3. Verified the database connection by running 'SELECT 1;' in the PostgreSQL console, confirming the database was unreachable. 4. Restarted the Inventory Service pod using 'kubectl rollout restart deployment/inventory-service'. 5. Monitored the service's availability with 'kubectl get pods -n inventory' and confirmed the pod was running. 6. Validated the API endpoint's responsiveness by sending a GET request to https://inventory-api.example.com/equipment-options using curl. 7. Reconfigured the Sales Agent's access rights via the CRM system's administrative panel to ensure proper permissions for equipment selection. The onboarding process was resumed once the Inventory Service was fully operational and the Sales Agent's permissions were correctly set.

short_description: Equipment Configuration Freeze on Legacy Browser
description: While trying to onboard an additional location for an existing merchant ID, the Sales Agent encountered a hardware issue with the POS terminal, preventing the configuration process. This affected the Sales Agent's ability to complete the onboarding for the merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that began with isolating the root cause of the equipment configuration freeze on the legacy browser. Initial diagnostics involved checking the network latency using the ping and traceroute commands to identify potential bottlenecks. The network infrastructure was found to be experiencing high latency, particularly between the POS terminal and the backend configuration server. The team used Wireshark to capture and analyze network traffic, which revealed that the legacy browser was generating excessive HTTP requests due to an outdated session management protocol. To mitigate this, Quality of Service (QoS) settings were adjusted on the core router (Cisco Catalyst 9500 series) to prioritize TCP/IP traffic associated with the configuration process. Additionally, the session timeout parameters were modified in the authentication service (OAuth 2.0) to accommodate the legacy browser's slower response times. The team also implemented a temporary workaround by enabling the browser's developer tools to monitor and throttle network requests, which helped in reducing the number of failed requests. Finally, a patch was applied to the POS terminal's firmware to enhance compatibility with the legacy browser's rendering engine, ensuring smoother data submission without timeouts.

short_description: Network connectivity issue preventing location addition
description: Sales Agent raised a concern that the merchant data being displayed in the Sales UI is showing incorrect information not matching the actual details provided.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. Initially, the Sales UI team performed a root cause analysis by examining the network connectivity logs and merchant data synchronization pipelines. The issue was traced to a misconfigured load balancer that was incorrectly routing merchant data requests to an outdated database replica, which contained stale or corrupted merchant information. To address this, the IT Support team executed the following steps: 1) Verified the load balancer configuration using `tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -tt` to capture and analyze network traffic patterns, confirming the incorrect routing. 2) Checked the database replication status with `SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G` on the MySQL server, which revealed that the replica was not properly synchronized with the master database. 3) Performed a manual data synchronization using `mysqldump --single-transaction --master-data=1 --lock-all-tables` to capture a consistent snapshot of the master database and restore it to the replica. 4) Reconfigured the load balancer to direct traffic to the updated master database instance, ensuring that all future merchant data requests would retrieve the correct information. Additionally, the fee calculation module was updated to include hardware compatibility checks, as previously mentioned, by modifying the `calculateFee()` function in the backend API to validate the merchant's hardware specifications against a centralized compatibility database. This change was implemented using a rolling deployment strategy with `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml` to minimize downtime. The Sales Agents were then able to accurately calculate fees and view correct merchant data in the Sales UI without encountering compatibility issues.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access onboarding portal for merchant ID
description: The Merchant reported a touchscreen malfunction on their device, making it impossible for them to e-sign the agreement in the Customer UI, hindering the onboarding progress.
resolution: The incident involved a Sales Agent experiencing an inability to access the onboarding portal for a specific merchant ID, primarily due to a touchscreen malfunction on the merchant's device.
