To resolve this, the module was updated to implement a retry mechanism with exponential backoff and a fallback to a cached state of the equipment configurations. Additionally, the team implemented a health check endpoint within the Sales UI to periodically validate the connection to the backend configuration service. This ensures that any future network issues would be detected early, allowing the system to either retry the operation or alert the support team. The resolution also included enhancing the error logging within the Sales UI to capture detailed information about the network status and any potential failures during data transmission. These changes were deployed during a maintenance window, and post-deployment, the Sales UI was tested with simulated network outages to verify that the new features were functioning as intended. The incident was confirmed to be resolved after the Sales Agent successfully completed the onboarding process for the merchant without any further disruptions.

short_description: Merchant unable to e-sign Agreement due to session timeout
description: Some merchants receive authentication errors when attempting to log in to the Customer UI to review and e-sign the Merchant Agreement, preventing access to the document.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically addressing the browser session and authentication state issues affecting the Customer UI. The initial diagnostic steps involved checking the browser console for JavaScript errors and network requests, which revealed intermittent 503 Service Unavailable errors during the PDF document loading phase. The support team then performed a deep dive into the browser's local storage and cookies, identifying a corrupted session token that was causing the authentication middleware to reject the request. Specific diagnostic commands included using 'curl -I https://customer-ui.example.com/api/v1/documents' to check the HTTP status codes and 'chrome://net-internals/#events' to monitor network activity. Additionally, the team inspected the server-side logs from the Authentication Service, which showed increased latency in token validation requests. To resolve the issue, the support team instructed the affected merchants to clear their browser cache and cookies via the browser settings (e.g., Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Clear browsing data > Cookies and site data). For more persistent cases, they advised using incognito mode or a different browser to bypass cached session data. The root cause was determined to be a combination of outdated session tokens and potential browser-specific caching anomalies, which were mitigated by ensuring the session management system was properly configured to handle token expiration and refresh mechanisms. The resolution was confirmed by retesting the Customer UI with a fresh browser session, which successfully loaded the PDF document without authentication errors.

short_description: Equipment selection dropdown not populating
description: Some merchants receive authentication errors when attempting to log in to the Customer UI to review and e-sign the Merchant Agreement, preventing access to the document.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic troubleshooting process that began with isolating the root cause of the equipment selection dropdown not populating. Initial diagnostics involved checking the frontend application logs for any client-side errors, which revealed a 401 Unauthorized error when attempting to fetch equipment data. This indicated an authentication failure at the API level. Further investigation uncovered that the authentication token used by the Customer UI was expiring prematurely due to a misconfigured token refresh mechanism in the Authentication Service. The token refresh interval was set to 5 minutes instead of the required 15 minutes, leading to session timeouts and subsequent authentication errors. To resolve this, the token refresh configuration in the Authentication Service was updated to align with the expected interval. Additionally, the backend API endpoints responsible for fetching equipment data were reviewed for any latency or caching issues. A performance analysis using the API monitoring tool 'Apigee' showed that the endpoints were experiencing occasional 503 Service Unavailable errors during peak hours, which were resolved by scaling the backend service horizontally. Finally, a full system test was conducted to ensure that all authentication flows and data fetching mechanisms were functioning correctly. The resolution included updating the token refresh interval, scaling the backend service, and implementing additional logging to monitor authentication events in real-time.

short_description: Sales UI not loading merchant data
description: Certain sales agents are facing an access permission error that is blocking them from configuring fees and services for specific merchants. This issue is hindering the customization of service offerings.
resolution: The issue with the Sales UI not loading merchant data was resolved through a structured diagnostic and remediation process. The initial step involved isolating the problem by verifying if the issue was specific to certain users or environments. This was done by checking the access logs of the Sales UI application, which revealed that the affected sales agents were encountering a 403 Forbidden error when attempting to access merchant configuration endpoints. Further investigation into the application's backend logs indicated that the error was related to role-based access control (RBAC) misconfigurations in the Authentication Service. The Authentication Service was responsible for validating the users' permissions against the required roles for accessing merchant data. Upon closer inspection, it was found that the fee calculation algorithm had a bug that caused it to incorrectly assign permissions to certain users, leading to the access permission error. To resolve this, the team first patched the fee calculation algorithm in the Sales UI backend service, ensuring that the correct permissions were assigned based on user roles. After the patch was deployed, the system was put through a series of regression tests to validate that the fee calculations were accurate and that the RBAC configurations were correctly enforced. Additionally, the team conducted a full system health check, including reviewing the Authentication Service's configuration and ensuring that all role-based access controls were properly aligned with the current user permissions. The resolution also included updating the access control policies to prevent similar issues in the future, ensuring that any changes to the fee calculation logic would not inadvertently affect user permissions. Finally, the Sales UI was reloaded, and the affected users were notified to reauthenticate to ensure their session tokens were refreshed, which resolved the access permission error and restored full functionality for configuring fees and services for specific merchants.

short_description: Hardware compatibility issue with fee calculation module
description: A Merchant is unable to e-sign the agreement as they are encountering a login error when trying to access the Customer UI, leading to a delay in the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by addressing the authentication service integration between the Customer UI and the backend systems. The root cause was identified through the following steps: 1) The support team first verified the error logs from the Customer UI application, which showed a 401 Unauthorized error when attempting to access the /api/v1/login endpoint. 2) They then checked the authentication service logs and found that the Sales Agent's account was not being properly synchronized with the authentication service due to a misconfigured LDAP synchronization rule. 3) The IT Support team used the `ldapsearch` command to validate the synchronization settings and confirmed that the Sales Agent's account was not being properly mapped to the authentication service's user database. 4) They then adjusted the LDAP configuration to ensure that the Sales Agent's account was correctly synchronized, which included updating the LDAP bind credentials and ensuring that the Sales Agent's group membership was properly reflected in the authentication service. 5) After the configuration changes, the support team performed a test login using the Sales Agent's credentials and confirmed that the authentication service was now able to validate the account, allowing seamless retrieval of the Merchant Agreement PDF. This fix ensured that the Sales Agent could access the Customer UI without encountering login errors, thus resolving the onboarding delay.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access fee configuration page
description: Merchants are unable to view the PDF Merchant Agreement after logging in to the Customer UI.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic troubleshooting approach targeting the authentication and session management components. Initially, the affected merchant's browser was checked for cached authentication tokens and session cookies using the browser's developer tools (Network tab, Application tab). We identified that outdated session cookies were being retained, preventing the secure establishment of a new session. Using the curl command, we verified the HTTP headers for the request to the /api/session endpoint, which showed a 401 Unauthorized error due to expired JWT token validation. The resolution involved clearing the browser's cache and cookies, specifically targeting the 'session_token' and 'auth_user' cookies. Additionally, we ensured the merchant's browser was updated to the latest version to resolve potential compatibility issues with the authentication middleware. The merchant was then guided through a complete logout and login process, which reinitialized the session and allowed access to the PDF Merchant Agreement. The authentication service logs were reviewed to confirm successful token issuance and validation, ensuring the session was secure and functional.

short_description: Equipment selection dropdown missing options
description: While configuring equipment for a new merchant, Sales Agent experienced network timeouts leading to delays in selecting the required hardware, affecting the efficiency of onboarding processes.
resolution: The incident was caused by a backend validation issue within the Equipment Configuration Service, which was leading to incomplete data submission when Sales Agents attempted to select hardware options. The root cause was identified through log analysis of the application server, where we observed 500 Internal Server Errors occurring when the dropdown options were not properly populated. The error logs indicated that the API endpoint responsible for fetching equipment options was returning an empty array due to a misconfigured database query. This query was not correctly joining the equipment catalog table with the available options table, resulting in an empty response. To resolve this, the database query was modified to ensure proper JOIN operations, and the API endpoint was updated to handle cases where no options were returned gracefully. Additionally, a client-side validation was implemented in the frontend to handle empty responses by displaying a default option or prompting the user for manual input. The fix was deployed through a rolling update on the backend servers, and the frontend code was redeployed to the staging environment for testing. Post-deployment, the system was monitored using Prometheus and Grafana for any anomalies, and no errors were recorded over a 24-hour period. The Sales Agent was able to successfully configure the equipment without any timeouts or missing options, restoring the onboarding process efficiency.

short_description: Merchant UI displaying blank screen post-login
description: Sales Agent experiences an issue where the submission button for the Merchant Agreement e-signature is unclickable, preventing progress to the processing stage.
resolution: Upon investigation, the root cause was identified as a misconfigured session timeout parameter within the Authentication Service, which was causing the UI to lose session context after login. The Sales Agent's session was being prematurely terminated due to the timeout threshold being set to 5 minutes, while the e-signature workflow required a minimum of 10 minutes to complete. To resolve this, the session timeout was adjusted to 15 minutes in the authentication service configuration file (auth-service.properties), and the session management module was updated to handle extended sessions gracefully. Additionally, the application server's session replication mechanism was configured to synchronize session data across all nodes to prevent session loss during load spikes. The network timeout issue was also addressed by optimizing the TCP keepalive settings on the backend servers, increasing the timeout threshold from 30 seconds to 2 minutes using the net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time parameter. This change ensured that the UI remained responsive during prolonged interactions. The fix was validated through automated regression tests, including simulated e-signature workflows and load testing with JMeter to ensure stability under high traffic. Finally, the incident was resolved by deploying the updated configuration to the production environment via a blue-green deployment strategy, minimizing downtime and ensuring zero service disruption.

short_description: Unable to select equipment for merchant
description: During the onboarding process for a new merchant location, Sales Agent selected equipment options but encountered a system issue where the selections were not being saved despite multiple attempts.
resolution: The issue was diagnosed as a frontend rendering anomaly within the merchant onboarding portal, specifically related to the dynamic form state management for equipment selection. Initial troubleshooting involved verifying the user's browser compatibility and clearing browser cache, as the form submissions were not persisting across page reloads. We executed a deep dive into the frontend codebase, focusing on the React component responsible for handling equipment selection. Using browser developer tools, we identified that the form data was being lost due to a race condition between the state updates and the backend API calls. The solution involved implementing a persistent state management pattern using Redux with middleware to ensure form data was stored in a centralized state before triggering API requests. Additionally, we added client-side validation to prevent duplicate submissions and introduced a debounce mechanism to handle rapid user interactions. The fix was deployed via a hotfix release, and the merchant was re-directed to the correct e-signature field within the PDF after the frontend state was properly synchronized with the backend.

short_description: Access permissions error for Merchant Agreement PDF
description: A Sales Agent is unable to access the fee configuration page in the Merchant Onboarding Application, hindering the ability to set up customized fees for a new merchant account.
resolution: The incident was attributed to a misconfiguration in the authentication service's access control policies, which were incorrectly restricting access to the fee configuration page for specific merchant account types. The root cause was identified through a detailed analysis of the access logs and user permissions database. A query was executed on the authentication service's database to extract all access control entries for the 'Merchant Onboarding Application' and cross-referenced with the user roles assigned to the Sales Agent. The diagnostic steps included checking the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration using the `audit-logs` command in the authentication service's CLI, which revealed that the 'Sales Agent' role lacked the necessary 'fee_config_access' permission. Additionally, the system's access control list (ACL) was reviewed using the `get-acl` command, which confirmed that the 'fee_config' endpoint was not properly mapped to the 'Sales Agent' role. The resolution involved updating the RBAC configuration by adding the 'fee_config_access' permission to the 'Sales Agent' role through the authentication service's management console. This change was propagated to the application servers via a configuration refresh command (`refresh-config --component auth-service`). Post-implementation, the Sales Agent was able to access the fee configuration page without any further issues. The incident also prompted a review of the access control policies to ensure that all user roles have the appropriate permissions for their responsibilities.

short_description: Access permission error for Merchant Agreement PDF upload
description: Intermittent occurrences of 500 internal server errors reported when making API calls for merchant onboarding, disrupting the data submission flow.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic process that began with analyzing the server logs and identifying the root cause of the 500 Internal Server Error. The first step involved reviewing the application server logs using the 'tail -f /var/log/apache2/error.log' command to monitor real-time errors. The logs revealed that the error occurred during the PDF upload process for merchant agreement documents, specifically when the API endpoint was called to store the file. Further inspection of the server's resource utilization showed that the disk I/O was at 95% capacity, indicating a potential storage bottleneck. To confirm this, the 'df -h' command was executed, which confirmed that the /var partition was nearly full. The next step was to investigate the cause of the disk space exhaustion. The system administrator checked the directory structure and found that the 'merchant_uploads' directory had accumulated a large number of temporary files and unprocessed PDFs, which were not being cleaned up after the upload process. To address this, a script was written to periodically clean up the temporary files using the 'find /var/merchant_uploads -type f -mtime +7 -exec rm -f {} \;' command. Additionally, the application's configuration was adjusted to use a dedicated storage partition for uploads, which was monitored using the 'du -sh /var/merchant_uploads' command to ensure consistent disk space availability. The issue was resolved after implementing these changes, and the API calls for merchant onboarding resumed without errors.

short_description: Equipment selection dropdown missing options
description: While configuring equipment for a new merchant, Sales Agent experienced network timeouts leading to delays in selecting the required hardware, affecting the efficiency of onboarding processes.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. The root cause was determined to be an outdated database schema in the Inventory Service, which did not include the 'ABC-2000' model. To resolve this, the following steps were executed: 1. Database schema audit using SQL queries to identify missing entries. 2. Verification of the database using the 'SELECT * FROM equipment_models' command, which confirmed the absence of 'ABC-2000'. 3. Execution of an INSERT statement to add the missing model to the database: INSERT INTO equipment_models (model_id, model_name, manufacturer) VALUES (1001, 'ABC-2000', 'ABC Corp'). 4. Database transaction logs were reviewed to ensure the update was successfully committed. 5. Post-remediation, the system was tested by attempting to select the 'ABC-2000' model from the dropdown, which now functioned correctly without network timeouts. Additionally, a scheduled database maintenance job was implemented to ensure future updates are automatically synchronized with the frontend dropdowns. The issue was resolved by ensuring the database contains the necessary equipment models, thereby eliminating the network timeouts and improving the onboarding process efficiency.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access fee configuration module
description: Merchants are experiencing network timeouts when trying to retrieve and e-sign the Merchant Agreement PDF. This is causing delays in the onboarding process as merchants are unable to proceed.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the root cause of the network timeouts experienced by merchants when accessing the fee configuration module. The initial step involved monitoring the application performance using the Application Performance Management (APM) tool, which revealed increased latency in the API calls to the merchant information database. Further investigation using the `curl` command to test the endpoint `/api/merchant/config` showed a 503 Service Unavailable error, indicating a backend service issue. The database logs were then examined, revealing a deadlock situation caused by a recent schema update that had not been properly rolled back. To resolve this, the database administrator executed a rollback of the schema change using the `ROLLBACK` command in PostgreSQL, which restored the previous state of the database. Additionally, a data refresh was performed using the `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` command on the relevant materialized view to ensure the Sales UI displayed the most up-to-date merchant information. The issue was confirmed to be resolved by retesting the API endpoint with `curl` and verifying that the Sales UI now loads the merchant configuration without timeouts. Finally, a preventive measure was implemented to ensure future schema changes are tested in a staging environment before deployment.

short_description: Intermittent latency spikes affecting API response times
description: Sales Agent noticed that any changes made to fees/services configurations for a merchant are not saving properly in the system.
resolution: Upon initial investigation, the IT Support team identified that the issue was not directly related to the network infrastructure as initially thought. Instead, the root cause was traced to a misconfiguration in the API gateway service responsible for handling the fee/service configuration updates. The team conducted a thorough analysis by monitoring API response times using Prometheus and Grafana, which revealed intermittent latency spikes during POST requests to the /api/configure endpoint. Further inspection of the application logs using ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) showed a pattern of 503 Service Unavailable errors when the system experienced high concurrent update requests. The team then performed a load test using JMeter to simulate peak traffic conditions, which confirmed the issue was a result of the API gateway's rate-limiting mechanism being triggered under high load. The resolution involved adjusting the rate-limiting thresholds in the gateway's configuration file (api-gateway.conf) and implementing a circuit breaker pattern using Hystrix to prevent cascading failures. Additionally, the backend service responsible for processing configuration updates was optimized by introducing asynchronous processing with RabbitMQ and reducing the number of database queries through caching with Redis. These changes were deployed during a maintenance window, and post-deployment monitoring confirmed a significant reduction in latency spikes, with the average response time dropping from 1200ms to 300ms.

short_description: Blank screen encountered post-login during agreement review
description: Upon successful login, the Merchant encounters a blank screen instead of the expected Merchant Agreement review interface.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that began with verifying the user's browser environment. The first step involved checking the browser's cache and cookies, which were cleared using the browser's built-in settings or via command-line tools such as 'chrome://settings/clearBrowserData' for Chrome or 'about:preferences#privacy' for Firefox. The user was instructed to clear the cache and cookies, then to restart the browser and attempt the login process again. If the issue persisted, the next diagnostic step was to inspect the browser's developer console (F12) for any JavaScript errors or network-related issues. This revealed potential problems with loading the PDF document or rendering the interface, which could be due to corrupted session data or misconfigured browser settings. To further isolate the issue, the user was directed to disable browser extensions that might interfere with the login process or page rendering. Additionally, the IT support team checked the server-side logs for the authentication service to identify if there were any errors related to session creation or PDF generation. The logs indicated that the session was being created successfully, but the PDF was not being rendered correctly, possibly due to a misconfigured MIME type or an issue with the PDF generation service. As a result, the user was advised to clear the browser cache and cookies, refresh the page, and ensure that the browser was up to date. The resolution confirmed that clearing the cache and cookies resolved the issue, allowing the PDF to load correctly and the Merchant Agreement review interface to display as expected. The support team also recommended regular maintenance of browser settings and periodic checks for browser updates to prevent similar issues in the future.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access merchant equipment options
description: Sales Agent experienced frequent network timeouts when selecting equipment for a merchant, causing delays in the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was escalated to the IT Support team upon receiving multiple reports from Sales Agents experiencing frequent network timeouts when attempting to select equipment options for a merchant. The root cause was identified as a misconfiguration in the equipment database linkage between the CRM system and the backend inventory service. To diagnose the issue, the team performed the following steps: 1. Checked the CRM system's database connection logs using the `pg_stat_activity` command in PostgreSQL to identify any failed connection attempts. 2. Analyzed the application logs in the /var/log/app.log directory, which showed timeout errors when querying the equipment database. 3. Performed a database schema check using the `psql -U admin -d equipment_db -c "\dt"` command to confirm the correct tables and relationships were in place. 4. Conducted a load test using JMeter to simulate multiple sales agents accessing the equipment selection interface simultaneously, which confirmed the database was not responding within the expected time frame. 5. Reviewed the network infrastructure using Wireshark to ensure there were no packet loss or latency issues between the CRM and the inventory service. 6. Checked the inventory service's configuration file (inventory-service.conf) and found that the database connection string was pointing to an outdated or incorrect database instance. 7. Verified the database server's status using the `systemctl status postgresql` command, which indicated the service was running normally. 8. Reconfigured the inventory service's connection string to point to the correct database instance and restarted the service using `systemctl restart inventory-service`. 9. Monitored the system performance using Grafana dashboards to ensure the changes resolved the issue. After the configuration was corrected, Sales Agents were able to access and select equipment options without experiencing network timeouts, and the onboarding process resumed smoothly.

short_description: Access denied error when trying to submit merchant data
description: Merchant data entered by Sales Agents in the Sales UI is not transferring to the Processing stage even after completion, halting the onboarding process for affected merchants.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that began with identifying the root cause of the access denied error. Initial diagnostics involved checking the Sales UI's access logs to trace the exact point of failure. The logs indicated that the Sales Agent role was being denied access to the fee configuration page, which is critical for transferring merchant data to the Processing stage. A thorough review of the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the Authentication Service revealed that the Sales Agent role lacked the necessary permissions to interact with the fee configuration API endpoint. To resolve this, the RBAC policy was updated to grant the Sales Agent role the appropriate permissions, including the 'configure_fees' action on the fee configuration resource. Additionally, a permissions audit was conducted using the 'auditlogs' command in the Identity Management System to ensure there were no other discrepancies. The fix was validated by re-testing the workflow with a sample merchant account, confirming that data submission now successfully transitions to the Processing stage. The resolution also included updating the role's access policy in the Identity Management System to prevent future occurrences of similar issues.

short_description: Access Rights Restriction
description: An issue arose where certain hardware configurations selected by Sales Agents were not compatible with the fee calculation module, resulting in incorrect fee estimations and potential financial discrepancies.
resolution: The incident, identified as INC00329, involved an incompatibility between specific hardware configurations selected by Sales Agents and the fee calculation module, leading to incorrect fee estimations. The root cause was traced to a synchronization issue between the fee configuration module and the additional location setup within the CRM system. The database team conducted a thorough investigation using SQL profiling tools such as MySQL Enterprise Monitor and PostgreSQL Query Analyzer to identify discrepancies in the synchronization process. They executed the following diagnostic commands: SELECT * FROM fee_configurations WHERE status = 'pending'; and EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM location_setup JOIN fee_configurations ON location_setup.id = fee_configurations.location_id; These commands revealed that the fee calculation module was not receiving updated location-based fee parameters from the database. The team then implemented a bidirectional synchronization script using Python's SQLAlchemy ORM to ensure real-time updates between the fee configuration module and the location setup. The script was tested in a staging environment using Docker containers to simulate production conditions, and it passed all integration tests. Additionally, the team configured a cron job to periodically check for any pending synchronization tasks and resolve them automatically. This ensured that the fee calculation module always had the most up-to-date fee parameters, thus eliminating the possibility of financial discrepancies.

short_description: Inability to configure services for additional location
description: Sales Agent received a duplicate merchant ID error message when attempting to add a new location for an existing merchant ID. This prevented the agent from successfully completing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by performing a targeted restart of the Sales UI server to address the duplicate merchant ID error during location configuration. Initial diagnostics involved checking the Sales UI server logs for any indications of data retrieval anomalies. The logs revealed intermittent failures in the merchant data fetch operation, specifically when attempting to retrieve existing merchant details for a given merchant ID. These failures were correlated with the duplicate merchant ID error, suggesting a possible race condition or data consistency issue in the backend database. To isolate the problem, we executed a series of diagnostic commands, including 'docker ps' to verify the container status of the Sales UI service, 'journalctl -u sales-ui.service' to review systemd logs, and 'curl -I http://sales-ui-api:8080/merchant/{merchantID}' to simulate API calls and assess the response status codes. The error logs indicated a 503 Service Unavailable status when the merchant ID was duplicated, pointing to a temporary backend service unavailability. To resolve this, we initiated a controlled restart of the Sales UI server using 'systemctl restart sales-ui.service'. This action cleared any transient state issues and re-established proper communication with the backend database, allowing the Sales UI to correctly validate merchant IDs and prevent the duplicate entry. Post-restart, we monitored the system using Prometheus and Grafana to ensure stability and confirmed that the error was resolved. Additionally, we implemented a temporary workaround in the Sales UI to enforce unique merchant ID validation at the frontend level, reducing the likelihood of duplicate submissions.

short_description: Intermittent connection issues while configuring services
description: A software bug in the fee calculation module is causing incorrect fees to be applied to merchant accounts by Sales Agents. Several merchants have been overcharged.
resolution: The incident was caused by a critical bug in the fee calculation module of the payment processing system, which resulted in incorrect fee application to merchant accounts. The root cause was identified through a combination of log analysis, database query auditing, and code review. The team began by examining the application logs for the affected period, which showed recurring errors related to fee calculation mismatches. Using the `grep` command with the pattern 'fee calculation error' on the application logs, the team found that the issue was occurring during the synchronization of transaction data between the payment gateway and the merchant database. Further investigation revealed that the fee calculation logic was incorrectly applying a flat rate instead of the dynamic per-transaction fee structure. The team then used the `pg_stat_activity` and `pg_locks` commands in PostgreSQL to monitor database activity and identify contention issues during the synchronization process. They also executed a `SELECT * FROM fee_calculations WHERE status = 'pending'` query to locate the affected transactions. After isolating the problematic code in the fee calculation module, the team implemented a fix that recalculated all pending transactions using the correct fee structure and ensured that future transactions would use the updated logic. Additionally, a database index was added to the `transactions` table on the `transaction_id` and `merchant_id` columns to improve query performance and prevent future contention. The resolution was verified by running a series of unit tests and integration tests, and by reprocessing the affected transactions to ensure that the fees were corrected. The incident was fully resolved, and all affected merchants were notified and provided with a detailed reconciliation report.

short_description: Merchant unable to e-sign agreement due to login error
description: An error occurs when a Sales Agent tries to save merchant data in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete information and hindered onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by a comprehensive investigation into the Sales UI's authentication flow. The team first validated the user's session state using the 'curl -I https://sales-ui.example.com/api/v1/merchant/data' command, which revealed a 401 Unauthorized error. This indicated an authentication token validation failure. The team then checked the Authentication Service logs at /var/log/auth-service.log and found entries with 'Invalid JWT signature' errors. Using the jwt.io debugger, they confirmed the token was malformed due to a missing header field in the token generation process. The root cause was traced to a recent update in the token generation logic that inadvertently removed the 'alg' header parameter. The fix involved reverting the token generation algorithm to the previous version while implementing a validation check to ensure the 'alg' header is present. Additionally, the team implemented a monitoring alert for JWT signature validation failures using Prometheus and Grafana. Finally, the Sales UI was redeployed with the updated authentication service, and all affected merchants were notified to re-authenticate and re-save their data.

short_description: Unable to link new location to existing merchant ID
description: Merchants encountered an access permission error while trying to upload and e-sign the Merchant Agreement PDF, preventing them from progressing to the processing stage and delaying onboarding completion.
resolution: The incident was caused by a rendering issue within the PDF viewer component of the merchant onboarding portal, which led to incorrect rendering of the e-signature fields and subsequent access permission errors. To resolve this, the following steps were executed: 1. Diagnosed the issue by analyzing user error logs and browser console outputs, which showed PDF viewer errors related to malformed PDF objects. 2. Performed a dependency audit of the PDF viewer component, identifying outdated libraries (e.g., PDF.js v2.10.371) that were incompatible with the latest browser security protocols. 3. Updated the PDF viewer to the latest version (PDF.js v3.4.120) via the application's package manager (npm install pdfjs-dist@3.4.120). 4. Rebuilt the frontend assets using Webpack 5, ensuring all static resources were properly cached and served. 5. Verified the fix by replicating the issue in a staging environment, using the same browser configurations and user credentials as the affected merchants. 6. Monitored system logs using ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) to confirm no further rendering anomalies. 7. Implemented a temporary workaround for users experiencing residual issues by clearing browser cookies and cache through the browser settings (chrome://settings/clearBrowserData). 8. Conducted a full regression test suite to ensure no other components were affected by the update. The resolution was successful, with all merchants able to upload and e-sign the agreement without access errors.

short_description: Access permission error for Merchant Agreement PDF upload
