Additionally, the Sales Agent's configuration was reviewed to ensure that the correct location ID was being used, and it was found that the existing location was indeed already present in the database under a different ID. The Sales Agent was instructed to update the existing location record instead of attempting to create a new one, which resolved the data loading issue. Finally, the Sales UI was restarted to clear any cached data that might have been causing the stale location information to persist.

short_description: Merchant Agreement e-signature field missing
description: Intermittent latency spikes were observed, causing delays in API responses during merchant data input by Sales Agents. This variability in response times impacted the overall speed of onboarding operations.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic process that began with monitoring the API response times using Prometheus and Grafana. Initial observations indicated intermittent latency spikes during merchant data input operations. The first step was to correlate the latency spikes with user activity by implementing a distributed tracing solution using Jaeger. This revealed that the delay was originating from the PDF viewer plugin used within the CRM application. Further investigation involved checking the plugin's version against the latest release on the vendor's repository, which showed that the installed version was outdated. To address this, the plugin was updated to the latest version (v3.2.1) via the package manager (npm). Additionally, we performed a deep dive into the plugin's rendering engine by analyzing the font rendering codebase, which was found to be inefficient for certain font types. We optimized the font loading process by implementing a font preloading mechanism using the <link rel="preload"> tag in the HTML head section. We also enabled font subsetting to reduce the size of the fonts being loaded. Finally, we conducted a load test using JMeter to simulate high traffic scenarios and ensure that the updated plugin did not introduce any new performance bottlenecks. The resolution was confirmed by monitoring the API response times over a 24-hour period, which showed a consistent reduction in latency from an average of 1.2 seconds to 0.3 seconds.

short_description: Incorrect fees calculation for bundled services
description: Sales Agent is unable to configure specific services for an additional location of a merchant due to a backend validation error, preventing the completion of the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was caused by a misconfiguration in the access control policies of the CRM system, which restricted the Sales Agents' ability to submit e-signature requests for bundled services. To resolve this, we performed the following steps: 1) Reviewed the access control policies in the CRM system using the 'audit-logs' command in the CRM CLI tool to identify the specific permissions that were missing. 2) Identified that the 'submit_e_signature' permission was not assigned to the Sales Agent role for the bundled services module. 3) Modified the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the CRM system by adding the 'submit_e_signature' permission to the relevant role. 4) Verified the fix by having a Sales Agent attempt to submit an e-signature request for a bundled service, which was successfully processed without any errors. 5) Monitored the system for any subsequent errors or access issues using the 'system_health_check' command in the CRM CLI tool. The resolution was confirmed to be successful, and the Sales Agent was able to complete the onboarding process for the additional location.

short_description: Unable to link new location to existing merchant ID
description: Some merchants receive authentication errors when attempting to log in to the Customer UI to review and e-sign the Merchant Agreement, preventing access to the document.
resolution: The incident was caused by a misconfigured load balancer and an overloaded authentication service, leading to intermittent timeouts and authentication errors for merchants attempting to access the Customer UI. The root cause was identified through a structured diagnostic approach. First, the network engineers executed a series of diagnostic commands such as `tcpdump` on the load balancer to capture and analyze traffic patterns, revealing that the authentication service was receiving an excessive number of requests during peak login hours. They also checked the authentication service logs using `journalctl -u authentication-service` and found numerous '503 Service Unavailable' errors, indicating backend overload. Additionally, the team used Wireshark to inspect the network packets and confirmed that the load balancer was not correctly distributing the traffic across the authentication service nodes. To resolve the issue, the load balancer configuration was updated to implement a more efficient round-robin algorithm with health checks enabled. The authentication service was scaled horizontally by adding two additional nodes, and the connection pool size was increased to handle the higher load. Furthermore, the team implemented rate limiting to prevent excessive login attempts from a single source. These changes were deployed during a maintenance window, and post-deployment, the authentication service was monitored using Prometheus and Grafana to ensure stability. Merchants were able to access the Customer UI without timeouts, and the authentication errors were resolved.

short_description: Intermittent Connectivity Issue During Equipment Selection
description: Sales Agent experiences an issue where the submission button for the Merchant Agreement e-signature is unclickable, preventing progress to the processing stage.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach involving multiple diagnostic steps and targeted code modifications. The Sales Agent reported that the submission button for the Merchant Agreement e-signature was unclickable, preventing progression to the processing stage. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the user's browser compatibility by checking the browser console for JavaScript errors. The developers executed the following diagnostic commands: 'curl -I https://merchant-agreement-service.example.com' to check the HTTP status codes and 'npm ls' to ensure all dependencies were up to date. The error logs indicated a 403 Forbidden error when attempting to access the e-signature endpoint, suggesting an authentication issue. Further inspection of the server-side logs revealed that the session token was not being properly validated due to a bug in the linking functionality between the CRM and the e-signature service. The developers identified a race condition in the token validation process where the session token was sometimes not being correctly passed between the frontend and backend services. To resolve this, a hotfix was implemented to ensure the token was explicitly passed in the request headers with the 'Authorization' field. Additionally, the developers modified the session management logic to include a token refresh mechanism every 5 minutes to prevent session expiration during critical operations. The hotfix was deployed via a rolling update to the e-signature service, and the Sales Agent was able to successfully submit the agreement after the deployment. Post-resolution, the team implemented automated tests to monitor the session token validation process and ensure that similar issues are detected early.

short_description: Intermittent connection issues while configuring services
description: A merchant is unable to log in to the Customer UI to review and e-sign the Merchant Agreement due to login credentials not being accepted.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and resolving a database inconsistency that was causing the false error message during the login process. The initial step involved verifying the user's credentials through the authentication service, which confirmed that the provided login details were valid. However, the system was returning an 'Invalid Credentials' error, indicating a mismatch between the expected and actual data in the database. To investigate further, the support team executed a series of SQL queries on the database to check the integrity of the user records. The query 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = 'merchant_user';' revealed that the user's location mapping was incorrectly stored, leading to the authentication service failing to validate the credentials correctly. The root cause was identified as a data migration error during a previous system update, which had incorrectly mapped the user's location information to a non-existent location entry. To resolve this, the database administrator executed a data correction script that updated the location mapping for the affected user, ensuring it aligned with the correct location in the database. This correction allowed the authentication service to validate the credentials accurately, resolving the login issue. Additionally, a database consistency check was performed using the 'CHECK TABLE users' command to ensure no other records were affected by the same inconsistency. The incident was resolved by 2023-10-15T14:30:00Z, and the user was able to log in successfully to the Customer UI to proceed with the Merchant Agreement review and e-signing process.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access merchant equipment options
description: Sales Agent experiences an issue where the submission button for the Merchant Agreement e-signature is unclickable, preventing progress to the processing stage.
resolution: The issue was diagnosed through a systematic approach involving multiple diagnostic steps. Initially, the support team verified the problem by replicating the issue in a controlled environment using the same browser and session credentials as the affected user. This confirmed that the problem was not isolated to a single user's environment. Next, the team performed a network latency check using the 'traceroute' command and observed increased latency between the user's endpoint and the backend server hosting the Merchant Agreement e-signature module. This indicated potential network routing inefficiencies. The team then analyzed the server-side logs using the 'tail -f' command on the application server, which revealed frequent timeout errors in the equipment selection module (specifically, 'TimeoutException: Connection timeout to /api/equipment/select'). This confirmed that the issue was not with the client-side browser but with the server-side processing of the equipment selection request. To resolve the issue, the team optimized the network routing by reconfiguring the BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) settings on the core routers, which rerouted traffic through a more stable and lower-latency path. Additionally, the team implemented a load balancing strategy using HAProxy to distribute the traffic more evenly across the backend servers, reducing the load on the primary server and minimizing timeout occurrences. The resolution also included an update to the application's timeout thresholds to better accommodate potential network fluctuations, ensuring that the system remains responsive under varying network conditions. These changes were validated through a series of automated tests using JMeter to simulate high user traffic and ensure that the system could handle peak loads without performance degradation. Finally, a post-resolution review was conducted to analyze the root cause and implement long-term monitoring solutions, such as integrating Prometheus and Grafana for real-time network and application performance monitoring.

short_description: Network timeout during equipment selection process
description: An error occurs when a Sales Agent tries to save merchant data in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete information and hindered onboarding process.
resolution: Upon receiving the incident report for INC00323, the IT Support team immediately initiated a thorough investigation into the network timeout issue occurring during the equipment selection process in the Sales UI. The first step was to isolate the problem by checking the connectivity between the Sales UI application servers and the backend systems. Using the ping and traceroute commands, we confirmed that there was a latency spike between the Sales UI frontend and the merchant data repository. Further diagnostic checks revealed that the network interface card (NIC) on the primary load balancer was experiencing intermittent packet loss, which was causing the timeout errors when Sales Agents attempted to save merchant data. To validate this, we executed the 'tcpdump' command on the affected load balancer to capture and analyze the network traffic, which showed fragmented packets and retransmissions indicative of a hardware failure in the NIC. The Network Ops team was then escalated to replace the faulty NIC with a redundant one, ensuring that the network path was restored. Additionally, we performed a deep dive into the system logs using the 'journalctl' command on the Linux-based servers, which highlighted intermittent connectivity issues and confirmed the hardware failure. Once the new NIC was installed, we conducted a series of connectivity tests, including 'iperf' for bandwidth testing and 'mtr' for routing path monitoring, to ensure that the network was stable and the timeout issue was resolved. The Sales UI was then retested with the Sales Agents, and the issue was successfully resolved, allowing for the complete submission of location data for the merchant ID without any further timeout errors.

short_description: Error message 'Invalid Signature' when attempting to e-sign Agreement
description: Merchants are unable to view the PDF Merchant Agreement after logging in to the Customer UI.
resolution: The incident was resolved by addressing a backend database synchronization error that was preventing configuration saves, which in turn caused the 'Invalid Signature' error when attempting to e-sign the Agreement. The root cause was identified through a combination of log analysis, database query inspection, and API monitoring. The team began by checking the application logs for any relevant error messages or stack traces related to the e-signature process. The logs indicated that the system was failing during the signature validation phase, specifically when attempting to verify the digital signature against the stored document hash. Further investigation revealed that the database synchronization process was not updating the document metadata in real-time, leading to a mismatch between the document's expected hash and the actual hash stored in the database. To diagnose this issue, the support team executed the following steps: 1. Inspected the database tables related to the document storage and metadata, using SQL queries such as SELECT * FROM document_metadata WHERE document_id = '12345'; 2. Checked the synchronization logs for any errors or delays using the command 'tail -f /var/log/sync_service.log'; 3. Monitored the API calls related to the e-signature process using tools like Postman and Wireshark to capture the HTTP requests and responses. The team then implemented a fix by optimizing the database synchronization process, ensuring that all document metadata updates were propagated in real-time. This involved modifying the synchronization service to use a more robust locking mechanism and increasing the frequency of sync intervals. Additionally, the team added a health check endpoint to the API that could be used to validate the synchronization status in real-time. Finally, the system was tested by simulating the e-signature process and verifying that the digital signature was correctly validated against the updated document hash.

short_description: Access permission error preventing merchant fee configuration
description: Merchant experiencing issues with loading the Merchant Agreement PDF for review and e-signing.
resolution: The incident was resolved by addressing a rendering issue with the PDF viewer component that was causing the merchant agreement PDF to fail to load properly, leading to access permission errors. The root cause was identified through a detailed analysis of the system logs and user reports, which indicated that the PDF viewer was not correctly handling certain PDF file structures, particularly those containing embedded fonts and advanced formatting. To resolve this, the PDF viewer software was updated to the latest version, which included improved rendering capabilities and enhanced compatibility with modern PDF standards. The update process involved downloading the latest version from the vendor's repository, verifying the integrity of the package using SHA-256 checksums, and deploying the update through the organization's package management system. Additionally, a rollback plan was prepared in case the update introduced new issues. After deployment, the system was monitored for a period of 48 hours to ensure stability and to confirm that the issue was resolved. The final confirmation came from user testing, where merchants were able to successfully load and review the PDF documents without any access permission errors.

short_description: Inaccurate service fee display on summary page
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to associate a new store location with an existing merchant ID, preventing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was investigated by first replicating the issue in a staging environment to confirm the problem's reproducibility. Using the provided test case, the QA team identified that the error occurred during the association of a new store location with an existing merchant ID. The root cause was traced to an outdated API endpoint in the merchant management module, which was incorrectly returning a stale service fee calculation. This led to the inaccurate display of service fees on the summary page. To resolve this, the development team reviewed the API integration code, specifically the 'calculateServiceFee' function, which was not correctly updating the fee structure based on the merchant's current subscription plan. The fix involved updating the API endpoint to fetch the latest fee details from the database using a query that joins the merchant subscriptions table with the fee structure table. The patch was then deployed to the production environment using a blue-green deployment strategy to minimize downtime. Post-deployment, the QA team conducted a regression test to ensure that the fix did not introduce any new issues. The incident was resolved successfully, and the service fee display is now accurate.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access onboarding portal for merchant ID
description: An error in the system caused incorrect fees to be applied to a merchant's account, resulting in financial discrepancies and potential loss of trust.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the root cause of the access issue. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the Sales Agent's access credentials and session validity using the 'auth-check' API endpoint. Logs from the Authentication Service revealed a misconfigured access control policy that was incorrectly restricting access to the onboarding portal for merchant ID 12345. The development team then conducted a code review of the equipment selection module, identifying a logical error in the access validation function that was failing to correctly authorize the Sales Agent's session. To resolve this, the team implemented a fix to the access control logic, ensuring proper session validation and role-based access permissions. The fix was deployed via a hotfix release to the staging environment, followed by a rollback of the previous faulty version. Post-deployment, the team performed automated regression testing using the 'access-validation-suite' test framework, confirming that the Sales Agent could now successfully reselect equipment for the new location. Additionally, a temporary workaround was implemented to enforce session re-authentication every 15 minutes to prevent similar issues in the future.

short_description: Sales UI not loading for new agent
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to onboard an additional location for merchant ID 12345. The system displayed a 'Duplicate Location' error message.
resolution: The incident was initiated by a Sales Agent attempting to onboard an additional location for merchant ID 12345. The system returned a 'Duplicate Location' error, preventing the agent from retrieving the agreement PDF. The initial investigation by network engineers revealed a bottleneck in the network configuration, which was causing timeouts during PDF retrieval. To diagnose the issue, the team executed a series of diagnostic commands, including `tcpdump` to capture network traffic and `netstat -an` to check for open ports and active connections. They also reviewed the system logs using `journalctl -u nginx` and found increased latency in the HTTP requests. Upon further analysis, it was determined that the network congestion was impacting the performance of the Sales UI, which is hosted on an NGINX server. The team optimized the network settings by adjusting the MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) values and implementing Quality of Service (QoS) policies to prioritize traffic related to the Sales UI. Additionally, they configured the NGINX server to use a reverse proxy setup, which helped in distributing the load more effectively. These changes significantly reduced the latency and resolved the 'Duplicate Location' error, allowing merchants to successfully retrieve the agreement PDF without timeouts. The resolution involved a combination of network optimization techniques and server configuration adjustments to ensure reliable performance of the Sales UI.

short_description: Network connectivity issue preventing location addition
description: Sales Agent encountered an error while trying to onboard an additional location for an existing merchant ID. The system failed to save the new location details.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the permission issue affecting the Sales Agent's account. The initial step involved verifying the user's access rights through the Identity and Access Management (IAM) system, specifically checking the role-based access control (RBAC) configuration. The Sales Agent's account was found to lack the necessary permissions to modify merchant location data, which is governed by the 'Merchant Onboarding API' under the CRM system. To confirm this, the following diagnostic steps were executed: 1) Reviewing the IAM audit logs for the Sales Agent's account to identify any recent changes or revoked permissions. 2) Executing a 'GET /api/merchant/{merchantID}/locations' request using the Sales Agent's API credentials to check the response status and payload. The response returned a 403 Forbidden error, indicating insufficient permissions. 3) Cross-referencing the Sales Agent's role with the 'Merchant Onboarding' policy in the IAM system, which revealed that the role did not include the 'update_locations' permission. 4) Checking the CRM system's access control list (ACL) to ensure that the Sales Agent's account was not excluded from the 'Location Management' feature. Once the root cause was identified, the resolution involved granting the Sales Agent the 'update_locations' permission via the IAM console, which was then synchronized with the CRM system through the 'IAM-CRM Sync Service'. This synchronization process typically takes 5-10 minutes, during which the Sales Agent's account was granted the necessary access. Post-implementation, the Sales Agent was able to successfully add the new location without encountering the error. Additionally, a temporary workaround was implemented to log all access attempts to the 'Merchant Onboarding API' with insufficient permissions, which will be reviewed during the next security audit to ensure no unauthorized access occurs.

short_description: Merchant unable to e-sign Agreement due to session timeout
description: An error in the system caused incorrect fees to be applied to a merchant's account, resulting in financial discrepancies and potential loss of trust.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that began with identifying the root cause of the session timeout and incorrect fee application. The initial diagnostic phase involved reviewing the system logs from the Authentication Service, which revealed that the session expiration mechanism was incorrectly configured. The session timeout duration was set to 15 minutes instead of the required 30 minutes, leading to premature termination of user sessions during the e-signing process. Additionally, the fee calculation module was found to be using outdated rate tables, which were not synchronized with the latest pricing rules. To address these issues, the development team first adjusted the session timeout configuration in the Authentication Service by modifying the 'session_timeout_seconds' parameter from 900 (15 minutes) to 1800 (30 minutes). They then implemented a patch to the fee calculation logic, ensuring it dynamically fetched the most current rate tables from the central pricing database. The fix was validated through automated regression tests, which included simulating e-signing sessions with varying durations to confirm the session persistence and accurate fee application. The Sales Agent was instructed to reselect the equipment and verify that the changes were successfully applied by checking the system logs and confirming the updated session timeout settings. Finally, a rollback plan was prepared in case the patch caused any unforeseen issues, and a monitoring alert was set up to track the session timeout metrics in real-time.

short_description: Inaccurate service fee display on summary page
description: Sales Agent reported inability to load Sales UI when onboarding a new merchant, impacting multiple ongoing merchant registrations.
resolution: The incident was caused by a bug in the service configuration module within the Sales UI application, which was preventing the correct loading of the service fee summary page. The development team conducted a thorough analysis of the issue by first replicating the problem in a staging environment. They used the following diagnostic steps: 1. Checked the server logs for any errors related to the Sales UI application, which revealed a 500 Internal Server Error when attempting to load the summary page. 2. Performed a code review of the service configuration module, identifying a misconfigured API endpoint that was incorrectly referencing a deprecated service fee calculation logic. 3. Used Postman to simulate API requests to the affected endpoint, confirming that the service fee calculation was returning an incorrect value due to a missing parameter in the request payload. 4. Inspected the database schema for the service fee configuration tables, ensuring that the required parameters were present and correctly formatted. 5. Conducted a load test using JMeter to confirm that the issue was not related to server performance or resource constraints. Once the root cause was identified, the development team implemented a code fix that corrected the API endpoint configuration and ensured the service fee calculation logic was properly integrated with the updated service configuration module. The fix was deployed to the production environment using a blue-green deployment strategy, which minimized downtime and ensured a smooth transition. Post-deployment, the team monitored the system using Prometheus and Grafana to confirm that the issue was resolved and that no further errors were occurring.

short_description: Hardware malfunction affecting equipment selection for merchants
description: Sales Agent encounters an issue where equipment selection dropdown menu is unresponsive for a specific merchant profile.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. Initially, the Sales Agent reported that the equipment selection dropdown menu was unresponsive for a specific merchant profile, which was identified as a frontend UI issue. The first step was to verify the issue by replicating the problem in a test environment. Using browser developer tools (Chrome DevTools), we inspected the dropdown element and observed that the JavaScript event listener for the 'change' event was not triggering. This indicated a potential issue with the frontend framework or a conflict with third-party libraries. Next, we checked the application logs for the merchant's session, which revealed an error related to the 'merchantProfile' object not being properly hydrated. This suggested a data inconsistency or a caching issue. We then performed a cache invalidation using Redis CLI with the command `FLUSHALL` to clear the cache, which temporarily resolved the issue. However, the problem reoccurred after a short period, indicating a persistent data inconsistency. To further diagnose, we executed a database query on the 'merchant_profiles' table to check for missing or corrupted records. The query `SELECT * FROM merchant_profiles WHERE merchant_id = 'M123456';` returned an incomplete record with missing fields. This confirmed that the database entry was corrupted. We then executed a data repair script to restore the merchant profile from a backup snapshot. After restoring the data, we reinitialized the frontend session using the 'Clear Session' API endpoint, which reset the UI state. Finally, we implemented a temporary workaround by adding a validation check in the frontend code to ensure the 'merchantProfile' object is fully populated before rendering the dropdown. The Sales Agent was then able to successfully configure the service fees for the merchant, and the onboarding process resumed. To prevent future occurrences, a scheduled database integrity check was added to the maintenance plan, and a frontend validation layer was introduced to handle data inconsistencies gracefully.

short_description: Merchant Agreement PDF displaying garbled text
description: An error occurs when a Sales Agent tries to save merchant data in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete information and hindered onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the sales UI application logs for any anomalies. The logs indicated a recurring error when saving merchant data, specifically a 'PDF Generation Error (Code: 503)' during the export phase. Further investigation revealed that the error was not originating from the frontend but was being propagated from the backend PDF generation service. A network trace using Wireshark showed intermittent connectivity issues between the Sales UI and the PDF generation microservice. The affected component was identified as the PDF Generation Service, which was running on an outdated server with insufficient memory allocation. A memory leak was confirmed via the 'top' command, which showed the service consuming over 90% of available RAM. The root cause was determined to be a corrupted configuration file in the '/var/opt/pdfgen/config.yaml' path, which was causing the service to fail during high-load scenarios. The corrupted configuration was replaced with a backed-up version, and the service was restarted. Additionally, the server's memory allocation was increased from 4GB to 8GB, and the service was configured to use a persistent volume for configuration storage. These changes restored the service's stability, allowing sales agents to save merchant data without encountering garbled text in the PDFs.

short_description: Merchant data displaying incorrectly
description: An error occurs when a Sales Agent tries to save merchant data in the Sales UI, leading to incomplete information and hindered onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the Sales UI's network connectivity using the 'ping' and 'traceroute' commands to identify potential network latency or packet loss. Subsequently, the Sales UI's backend API endpoints were tested using 'curl' to check for HTTP status codes and response times. Analysis of the application logs revealed intermittent 503 Service Unavailable errors originating from the Network Infrastructure component. Further investigation using Wireshark confirmed that the Sales UI was unable to establish a stable connection to the backend merchant data service due to a misconfigured load balancer. The load balancer was incorrectly routing traffic to a deprecated server cluster, which was experiencing high latency and incomplete data processing. The root cause was identified as a misconfigured load balancer in the Network Infrastructure, which was not properly directing traffic to the active merchant data service. The load balancer configuration was updated to route traffic to the correct backend servers, and the DNS records were validated to ensure proper domain resolution. Post-remediation, the Sales UI was tested again using automated scripts to verify data integrity and successful merchant data submission. The issue was fully resolved, allowing Sales Agents to save merchant data without any incomplete information.

short_description: Merchant UI displaying blank screen post-login
description: Despite Sales Agents configuring specific fees and services for a merchant in the Sales UI, these selections are not reflecting accurately in the final Merchant Agreement generated, causing discrepancies.
resolution: The issue was resolved by addressing the misconfiguration in the Authentication Service's access control policies, which were preventing the Sales Agent's account from retrieving the Merchant Agreement PDF. The root cause was identified through a series of diagnostic steps: first, we checked the Sales Agent's access permissions using the 'get_user_permissions' API endpoint, which revealed that the account lacked the 'read_merchant_agreement' privilege. Next, we reviewed the Authentication Service's role-based access control (RBAC) configuration using the 'audit_access_policies' command, which showed that the Sales Agent's role was not assigned the necessary permissions for retrieving the Merchant Agreement PDF. To resolve this, we updated the RBAC configuration by adding the 'read_merchant_agreement' privilege to the Sales Agent's role via the 'update_role_permissions' API. Additionally, we verified the changes by re-checking the access permissions using the 'get_user_permissions' API and confirmed that the Sales Agent could now retrieve the Merchant Agreement PDF without any issues. Finally, we monitored the system for any further discrepancies by analyzing the Authentication Service's access logs using the 'analyze_access_logs' tool, which showed no further unauthorized access attempts or permission-related errors.

short_description: Error saving merchant data in Sales UI
description: A software bug in the fee calculation module is causing incorrect fees to be applied to merchant accounts by Sales Agents. Several merchants have been overcharged.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic and remediation process. Initially, the Sales UI error was reported by multiple sales agents, who noted that when attempting to save merchant data, the system was applying incorrect fees. The first step was to isolate the issue by reproducing the error in a controlled environment. The development team used the Sales UI's debug logs (located in /var/log/sales-ui/debug.log) to trace the error flow. They identified that the fee calculation module, specifically the calculateFee() function in the FeeCalculator.java class, was incorrectly using a deprecated rate table that had been replaced by a new one during a recent deployment. The root cause was a misconfiguration in the application's configuration file (fee-configuration.properties), where the new rate table's path was not correctly specified. To address this, the operations team executed a rollback to the previous stable version of the fee calculation module using the deployment tool Ansible. They then applied a patch to the configuration file to point to the correct rate table path. After the patch was applied, the team performed a series of automated regression tests using the Jenkins CI/CD pipeline to ensure that the fee calculations were now accurate. Finally, the Sales UI was reloaded, and the system was monitored for 24 hours to confirm that the issue was fully resolved and no further errors were occurring.

short_description: Network timeout during equipment selection process
description: Sales Agent encountered a hardware compatibility issue while configuring fees for a merchant, leading to incorrect fee settings.
resolution: The incident was initiated by a network timeout error occurring during the equipment selection phase of the merchant onboarding process. The Sales Agent encountered an issue when attempting to configure fees for a merchant, which resulted in incorrect fee settings being applied. This problem stemmed from a communication failure between the frontend application and the backend API responsible for processing merchant data. The root cause was identified as a misconfigured API gateway that was intermittently dropping requests due to an overloaded load balancer. The team began by analyzing the application logs using the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) to trace the sequence of events. They discovered that the API endpoint responsible for fee configuration was returning a 503 Service Unavailable error when the request volume exceeded the predefined threshold. To diagnose further, the team executed the 'curl -v http://api.example.com/fee-configuration' command, which confirmed the intermittent connectivity issues. The network team was then engaged to investigate the load balancer configuration and discovered that the backend servers were not properly scaled to handle peak traffic. Additionally, the API gateway logs revealed that the rate-limiting rules were too restrictive, causing legitimate requests to be rejected. The resolution involved adjusting the load balancer settings to distribute traffic more evenly across the backend servers, increasing the maximum allowed request rate, and implementing a circuit breaker pattern in the frontend to handle transient failures gracefully. The API gateway was also reconfigured to allow higher throughput while maintaining security constraints. Once these changes were implemented, the network timeout issue was resolved, and the merchant data flow resumed without interruption. Post-resolution, the team conducted a load test using JMeter to ensure the system could handle the expected traffic volume, confirming that the modifications were effective.

short_description: Merchant unable to e-sign agreement
description: Merchants encountered an access permission error while trying to upload and e-sign the Merchant Agreement PDF, preventing them from progressing to the processing stage and delaying onboarding completion.
resolution: The incident was diagnosed as a routing issue affecting the stability of the merchant portal's connectivity. The network team initiated a thorough analysis by first checking the routing tables on the core routers using the 'show ip route' command. They identified that the default route was misconfigured, leading to intermittent connectivity issues when merchants accessed the portal. The team then performed a traceroute from the merchant's end to the portal's backend servers using the 'traceroute -T <server_ip>' command, which revealed packet loss and routing loops between the merchant's network and the portal's load balancer. To resolve this, the network team reconfigured the routing tables on the core routers to use a more stable and direct path to the portal's backend servers. They also implemented Quality of Service (QoS) policies to prioritize traffic related to the merchant portal. Additionally, they monitored the network performance using tools like Wireshark and PRTG Network Monitor to ensure that the issue was fully resolved and that there were no recurring routing problems. The resolution was verified by testing the portal's accessibility from multiple merchant locations and confirming that the access permission error was no longer occurring.

short_description: Incorrect fees calculation for bundled services
description: Sales Agent raised a concern that the merchant data being displayed in the Sales UI is showing incorrect information not matching the actual details provided.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach involving multiple stages of diagnosis, root cause analysis, and code implementation. The issue originated from the service fee calculation logic in the Sales UI, which was incorrectly displaying bundled service fees. To address this, the following steps were taken: 1) The development team conducted a code review of the fee calculation module, identifying a logic error in the aggregation of service fee rates. 2) They executed unit tests and integration tests to reproduce the issue, confirming that the calculation logic was not properly handling the bundling of multiple services. 3) The team then implemented a fix by revising the calculation algorithm to ensure that each service's fee was correctly aggregated based on its configuration. 4) After the code change, the team performed a full regression test suite to validate the fix across all relevant scenarios. 5) The updated code was deployed to the staging environment and validated against real-time data to ensure accuracy. 6) Finally, the fix was rolled out to the production environment, and the Sales UI was monitored for several hours to confirm that the fee breakdown now accurately reflected the configured fees. This resolution ensured transparency and accuracy in the fee breakdown presented to merchants, preventing potential revenue discrepancies and enhancing trust in the platform.

short_description: Critical Service Fee Configuration Failure
description: Merchant unable to locate the e-signature field within the Merchant Agreement PDF for completing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved by conducting a thorough analysis of the e-signature module's integration with the Merchant Agreement PDF rendering engine. The root cause was identified as a misconfiguration in the PDF template generation process, specifically a missing field definition for the e-signature area in the PDF document structure. Diagnostic steps included reviewing the PDF generation logs, analyzing the template rendering pipeline using the PDFKit library, and inspecting the database schema for the merchant agreement records. The error logs indicated a 'Field Not Found' exception during the PDF rendering phase. The fix involved updating the template configuration to include the e-signature field definition, ensuring the PDF rendering engine could correctly map the signature area. Additionally, the system was tested with a sample merchant account to validate the fix, and the e-signature functionality was restored without encountering the 'Invalid Signature' error. The resolution also included implementing a monitoring script to periodically check the template configuration and alert on any future misconfigurations.

short_description: Merchant Agreement e-signature field missing
description: Sales Agent reported inability to retrieve merchant information through the REST API, impacting onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic troubleshooting process that began with isolating the root cause of the merchant agreement e-signature field missing issue. The initial step involved reviewing the REST API logs to identify any anomalies or error patterns. The team used the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) to aggregate and analyze API request and response data. Upon inspection, it was observed that the API endpoint responsible for retrieving merchant information was returning a 400 Bad Request error when attempting to access the e-signature field. Further investigation revealed that the API code had a bug in the data parsing logic, specifically in the deserialization of JSON payloads. The error stemmed from an incorrect field name mapping in the API's model layer, where the e-signature field was being referenced as 'esign' instead of the correct 'esignature'. This mismatch caused the API to fail to retrieve the field, resulting in the missing data. To confirm the issue, the development team executed unit tests using Postman to simulate API requests and validate the response structure. The test results confirmed the field name discrepancy. The fix involved updating the API model to correct the field name mapping and applying a patch to the production environment. Additionally, a rollback plan was prepared in case the patch introduced new issues, and a rollback was executed using the version control system (Git) to revert to the previous stable version if necessary. The patch was deployed using a CI/CD pipeline, ensuring minimal downtime and maintaining system stability. Post-patch, the team monitored the API's performance using Prometheus and Grafana to ensure that the issue was fully resolved and no new errors were introduced.

short_description: Sales UI not loading merchant data
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to add a new POS system for a high-volume merchant, leading to delays in onboarding process.
resolution: Upon investigation, the Sales Agent reported that when attempting to add a new POS system for a high-volume merchant, the Sales UI was displaying an error message related to data loading failure. Initial diagnostics revealed that the error was not originating from the front-end application or the network infrastructure. The error log analysis indicated a database inconsistency, specifically an incorrect location mapping entry for the merchant's new POS system. The database schema in question was the 'merchant_location' table within the 'sales_db' database. Further inspection of the database using the MySQL command-line interface and the 'SELECT * FROM merchant_location WHERE merchant_id = 12345;' query confirmed the presence of a stale entry with an invalid geographic coordinate set. This entry was causing the Sales UI to fail when attempting to validate the location against the geospatial index. To resolve the issue, the database administrator executed a 'DELETE FROM merchant_location WHERE merchant_id = 12345 AND location_id = 67890;' command to remove the invalid entry. Additionally, a 'REPAIR TABLE merchant_location;' was executed to ensure data integrity. After these changes, the Sales Agent was able to successfully add the new POS system without encountering the error. The incident was resolved by correcting the database inconsistency and ensuring the location mapping was accurate, allowing the onboarding process to proceed without delays.

short_description: PDF not loading for Merchant Agreement review
description: Merchants encountering access permissions error when trying to view the Merchant Agreement PDF for e-signing, causing delays in agreement completion.
resolution: The incident was caused by a database synchronization error between the merchant management system and the document storage service, leading to incomplete or corrupted metadata for the Merchant Agreement PDF files. The root cause was identified through a systematic diagnostic process involving the following steps: 1) Checked database replication logs for the 'merchant_documents' table, which showed delayed syncs and missing entries for certain merchant IDs. 2) Performed a database consistency check using the 'CHECK TABLE merchant_documents' command in MySQL, revealing 12 rows with missing 'document_hash' fields. 3) Analyzed the application logs for the document service, which indicated that the 'fetch_document' API endpoint was returning 404 errors for these missing entries. 4) Verified the database schema version against the application's expected schema, confirming that the 'document_hash' field was not properly migrated during a recent schema update. The resolution involved: 1) Reinitializing the database replication for the 'merchant_documents' table, ensuring all entries are synchronized with the document storage service. 2) Manually correcting the missing 'document_hash' entries using a custom SQL script that recalculates the hash based on the document content. 3) Implementing a database trigger to automatically update the 'document_hash' field whenever a new document is uploaded, ensuring data integrity. 4) Enhancing the 'fetch_document' API endpoint to handle missing hashes by redirecting to the document storage service's fallback URL. 5) Conducting a full system test to verify that all merchants can now access their agreement PDFs without access permissions errors, and confirming that the database synchronization is now operating within acceptable latency thresholds.

short_description: Intermittent data loss in merchant review stage
description: Merchant data entered by Sales Agents in the Sales UI is not transferring to the Processing stage even after completion, halting the onboarding process for affected merchants.
resolution: The intermittent data loss issue in the merchant review stage was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the Sales UI session state using browser developer tools to inspect cookies and local storage for any session expiration or token invalidation issues. We confirmed that the Sales Agent's session was valid but the data transfer to the Processing stage was failing due to a misconfigured API endpoint in the onboarding portal's backend. The affected API endpoint was identified using the curl command: curl -I -X GET https://onboarding-api.example.com/merchant/data-transfer, which returned a 503 Service Unavailable error. Further investigation revealed that the data transfer was being blocked by a misconfigured load balancer rule in the Network Infrastructure, which was incorrectly routing requests to a deprecated backend instance. The issue was resolved by updating the load balancer configuration to route requests to the correct active backend service and ensuring that the API endpoint was properly registered in the service discovery registry. Additionally, we validated the integrity of the data transfer process by implementing a temporary data validation script using Python's requests library to simulate the data transfer and confirm successful endpoint communication. Finally, we performed a rollback of the Sales Agent's access credentials to ensure that the user's session state was not compromised and that the onboarding process could resume seamlessly.

short_description: Network connectivity issue preventing location addition
description: Intermittent latency spikes were observed, causing delays in API responses during merchant data input by Sales Agents. This variability in response times impacted the overall speed of onboarding operations.
resolution: Upon initial assessment of the incident, the IT Support team identified that the intermittent latency spikes were primarily impacting the Sales Agent's device network connectivity, specifically during API interactions required for merchant data input. The first step in the resolution process was to perform a thorough network diagnostic to isolate the root cause. Using the `ping` and `traceroute` commands, we tested connectivity to the backend API endpoints and observed inconsistent latency values between 200-800 ms during peak usage periods. Further investigation revealed that the Sales Agent's device was experiencing packet loss and jitter, which was confirmed using the `mtr` tool, which provided a detailed view of the network path and identified a bottleneck at the local network gateway. The team then conducted a deep dive into the device's network configuration, checking for any misconfigured Quality of Service (QoS) settings or firewall rules that could be affecting traffic prioritization. No misconfigurations were found. The next step was to perform a hardware inspection of the Sales Agent's device, which revealed that the network interface card (NIC) was experiencing intermittent failures, likely due to overheating and physical wear. To resolve this, the malfunctioning NIC was replaced with a high-performance, enterprise-grade model, which significantly reduced latency to below 50 ms. Additionally, the team implemented a network monitoring solution using PRTG Network Monitor to continuously track latency and packet loss metrics, ensuring early detection of similar issues in the future. The Sales Agent was also provided with updated network drivers and a script to periodically check for connectivity issues using `curl` and `ping` commands, which would automatically alert the IT team if any anomalies were detected. These measures ensured seamless continuation of the merchant data input process and restored the required network performance for onboarding operations.

short_description: Sales UI not loading merchant data
description: Sales Agent encountered an error while configuring POS terminals for a merchant, leading to incorrect settings. Merchant transactions are impacted.
resolution: Upon initial investigation, the Sales UI's inability to load merchant data was traced to a misconfigured POS terminal integration within the Sales Application's backend module. The error logs from the application server indicated a timeout in the 'equipmentSelection' microservice, specifically during the 'fetchMerchantData' API call. To diagnose, we executed the following steps: 1. Checked the application server logs using 'tail -f /var/log/app-server.log' which showed 504 Gateway Timeout errors when accessing the equipment selection module. 2. Performed a network latency check using 'mtr -r equipment-selection-service' and found increased latency between the Sales UI frontend and the equipment selection service. 3. Analyzed the microservice's health endpoint at 'http://equipment-selection-service/health' and discovered it was returning a '503 Service Unavailable' status due to high CPU utilization. 4. Inspected the database connection pool metrics for the equipment selection service using Prometheus and found that the pool was exhausted, leading to connection timeouts. The root cause was identified as an unoptimized database query in the 'fetchMerchantData' endpoint, which was causing excessive load on the database and resulting in timeouts. The resolution involved optimizing the query by adding appropriate indexes to the 'merchant_equipment' table, specifically on the 'merchant_id' and 'equipment_type' columns. Additionally, we implemented a circuit breaker pattern using Hystrix to prevent cascading failures when the database is under heavy load. The service was restarted, and the query performance improved from 8.2 seconds to 0.3 seconds, resolving the timeout issues and significantly enhancing system responsiveness.

short_description: Fee configuration not reflecting for additional location
description: Merchants are experiencing network timeouts when trying to retrieve and e-sign the Merchant Agreement PDF. This is causing delays in the onboarding process as merchants are unable to proceed.
resolution: The incident was resolved by addressing a font rendering issue within the PDF viewer plugin that caused text to not display correctly in the Merchant Agreement PDF. The root cause was identified through customer-reported network timeouts and subsequent analysis of the PDF viewer's behavior. The diagnostic process involved checking the PDF viewer's plugin version, reviewing error logs from the application server, and analyzing browser console outputs. The team used the `chrome://plugins/` interface to inspect the plugin's status and confirmed that the outdated version was not compatible with the latest PDF standards. Further investigation revealed that the font rendering issue was causing the PDF viewer to hang during the rendering process, which led to network timeouts as the browser attempted to load the PDF. To resolve this, the plugin was updated to the latest version (v3.5.2) using the package manager `npm install pdf-viewer-plugin@latest`. The update included enhanced font rendering capabilities and improved compatibility with modern PDF specifications. Post-update, the team performed a series of regression tests, including loading the PDF in different browser environments and simulating high-traffic scenarios to ensure stability. The resolution was confirmed by monitoring the application's performance metrics and verifying that the network timeouts had been eliminated. Additionally, the team implemented a scheduled update check for the plugin to prevent similar issues in the future.

short_description: Fees Calculation Mismatch for Specific Equipment Bundle
description: Merchant experiencing issues with loading the Merchant Agreement PDF for review and e-signing.
resolution: The incident was resolved by addressing a critical database synchronization error that was preventing the configuration saves required for the Merchant Agreement PDF generation. The diagnostic process began with a detailed review of the application logs, which showed repeated entries of "DatabaseSyncException: Failed to sync configuration data for bundle ID 12345". Using the database monitoring tool "DBWatch", we identified that the synchronization process between the primary database and the replication slave was failing due to a corrupted index on the "equipment_bundles" table. The corruption was traced back to an unhandled exception in the batch update script that was executed during a scheduled maintenance window. To resolve the issue, the team performed the following steps: 1. Executed a database consistency check using the "pg_verify" tool on the PostgreSQL instance. 2. Rebuilt the corrupted index using the command: "REINDEX INDEX equipment_bundles_bundle_id_idx;". 3. Verified the fix by running a series of configuration save tests through the API endpoint /api/v1/config/save, which returned a 200 OK status. 4. Monitored the synchronization process using the "DBWatch" tool for 24 hours to ensure no further errors occurred. The resolution confirmed that the Merchant Agreement PDF could now be generated and loaded correctly for the affected equipment bundles.

short_description: Merchant Agreement e-signature field missing
description: Multiple Sales Agents experienced intermittent network connection problems while configuring services for merchants, leading to incomplete configurations and frustration.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the UI responsiveness and configuration synchronization issues affecting the merchant agreement e-signature functionality. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the network connectivity of the Sales Agents' workstations using the 'ping' and 'traceroute' commands to confirm there were no intermittent network outages. The Network Operations team then checked the backend API endpoints responsible for loading the e-signature configuration, discovering that the UI was failing to synchronize with the backend service due to a timeout in the AJAX requests. The team analyzed the server logs for the e-signature service and identified a pattern of 504 Gateway Timeout errors, which indicated that the backend service was not responding within the expected time frame. To isolate the issue, the team performed a controlled restart of the e-signature service container, which reset the connection pool and resolved the timeout issue. Additionally, the team implemented a temporary workaround by adjusting the timeout threshold in the frontend JavaScript code to allow for longer response times during periods of high load. Finally, a full system restart of the UI components was executed to clear any lingering session state or cached data that might have contributed to the problem, restoring full functionality for the merchant to complete the e-signature process.

short_description: API endpoint returning 500 error for merchant creation
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to add a new POS system for a high-volume merchant, leading to delays in onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach that began with identifying the root cause of the 500 Internal Server Error encountered during the merchant creation process via the Sales UI. The initial step involved reviewing the application logs from the Sales UI service, which revealed that the error occurred when attempting to submit the merchant creation request. The logs indicated a NullPointerException in the equipment selection module, specifically when the system attempted to access a null object reference during the processing of the POST /api/merchants endpoint. To diagnose further, the support team executed a stack trace analysis using the application's logging framework, which pointed to the EquipmentSelector class in the Sales UI's backend module. The team then conducted a code review of the EquipmentSelector class, identifying that the module was not properly validating the input parameters before attempting to process the request. This led to a situation where the system attempted to access a null object when the required parameters were missing or invalid. To resolve the issue, the development team implemented a series of input validation checks within the EquipmentSelector class, ensuring that all required parameters were present and correctly formatted before proceeding with the request processing. Additionally, the team enhanced the error handling mechanism to provide more detailed error messages to the client, which would help in identifying the root cause of similar issues in the future. The fix was deployed to the production environment through a rolling update, and the system was monitored for any potential regressions. Post-deployment, the Sales UI was tested with a set of predefined test cases to ensure that the issue was fully resolved and that no new issues were introduced. The resolution also included updating the documentation for the EquipmentSelector class to include the new validation logic and error handling procedures, ensuring that future developers are aware of the changes and can maintain the codebase effectively.

short_description: Login credentials not working for merchant
description: Sales Agent encountered an issue where a specific POS terminal model, 'ABC-2000', could not be selected while configuring equipment for a merchant.
resolution: The incident was resolved by systematically diagnosing and addressing the issue with the POS terminal model 'ABC-2000' during the merchant onboarding process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the terminal's compatibility with the current system configuration. The team executed a series of diagnostic commands, including checking the terminal's firmware version using the command 'get_terminal_version' and ensuring it matched the supported version listed in the system's compatibility matrix. The logs from the terminal's communication interface were analyzed using the 'tail -f /var/log/terminal_logs' command, which revealed an authentication error related to the merchant's credentials. Further investigation showed that the POS terminal's authentication service was failing to validate the merchant's login credentials due to a misconfigured session token expiration setting. To resolve this, the team adjusted the session token expiration parameter in the 'auth_config.json' file, setting it to a higher value of 3600 seconds (60 minutes). Additionally, the terminal's authentication service was restarted using the command 'sudo systemctl restart auth_service' to apply the changes. The team also implemented a script to automatically validate the terminal's credentials during the onboarding process, which checks the 'merchant_credentials' table in the database for valid entries and ensures the terminal's configuration aligns with the merchant's profile. These changes were tested in a staging environment before deployment to ensure stability and prevent future occurrences of the issue.

short_description: Sales Agent unable to access fee configuration module
description: Merchant unable to locate the e-signature field within the Merchant Agreement PDF for completing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was triggered by a backend synchronization issue between the Merchant Agreement PDF generation service and the fee configuration module. Upon initial investigation, the Sales Agent reported that the e-signature field was missing from the generated PDF, which is critical for the onboarding process. The root cause was identified as a misalignment between the fee configuration database and the PDF generation engine. The synchronization process was manually initiated using the `sync_fee_config` command, which is part of the backend service's maintenance scripts. This command triggered a full re-synchronization of the fee configuration data from the database to the PDF generation service. Diagnostic steps included checking the system logs for the `pdf_generator` service, which revealed a timestamp mismatch between the database and the service's internal clock. Additionally, the `db_consistency_check` tool was executed to verify data integrity, and it confirmed that the fee configuration records were present but not properly indexed. The resolution involved not only executing the manual sync but also implementing a scheduled sync task to prevent future occurrences. The Sales Agent confirmed that the fees and services configurations were now accurately displayed, and the e-signature field was successfully included in the latest generated PDF.

short_description: Payment terminal integration failure during merchant setup
description: An issue arose where certain hardware configurations selected by Sales Agents were not compatible with the fee calculation module, resulting in incorrect fee estimations and potential financial discrepancies.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic approach to address the integration failure between the payment terminal hardware configurations and the fee calculation module. Initially, the team conducted a root cause analysis by reviewing the system logs and error messages generated during the merchant setup process. The logs indicated that certain hardware configurations were not recognized by the fee calculation module, leading to incorrect fee estimations. The team used the 'tail -f /var/log/syslog' command to monitor real-time log entries and identified a pattern of errors related to incompatible hardware models. Next, the team performed a compatibility check by querying the database using SQL commands such as 'SELECT * FROM hardware_configurations WHERE compatibility_status = 'incompatible'' to isolate the problematic configurations. The database query results were cross-referenced with the fee calculation module's API documentation to determine the specific parameters causing the mismatch. Following this, the team implemented a patch to the fee calculation module by modifying the configuration parsing logic to handle the incompatible hardware models gracefully. The patch was tested in a staging environment using automated unit tests and integration tests to ensure it did not introduce new issues. Once validated, the patch was deployed to the production environment using a rolling update strategy to minimize downtime. Post-deployment, the team monitored the system using Prometheus and Grafana to ensure the fee calculation module was functioning correctly and that no further errors were being logged. Additionally, the team updated the Sales Agent's interface to include a compatibility check before allowing them to select hardware configurations, preventing similar issues in the future.

short_description: Network timeout during merchant equipment selection
description: During the onboarding process for an additional location, the Sales Agent received an error message stating 'Location already exists' even though it's a new location being added. This issue caused confusion and delays in completing the merchant setup.
resolution: The incident was resolved by conducting a thorough investigation into the 'Location already exists' error encountered during the onboarding process for a new merchant location. The initial step involved verifying the database integrity to ensure there were no duplicate entries for the new location. Using a SQL query, the database administrator executed a SELECT * FROM locations WHERE location_name = 'New Location Name'; to confirm the absence of existing records. Further, the IT Support team examined the application logs for the CRM system, specifically focusing on the onboarding module, to identify any potential race conditions or concurrent updates that might have caused the error. The log analysis revealed that the error occurred when multiple Sales Agents attempted to add the same location simultaneously, leading to a race condition in the database transaction. To resolve this, the database schema was updated to include a unique constraint on the location_name field, ensuring that only one entry could exist for each location name. Additionally, the application code was modified to implement a retry mechanism with exponential backoff for duplicate key errors, preventing the error from occurring in the future. The Sales Agent role's access permissions were also reviewed and corrected to ensure proper access to the fee configuration page, enabling seamless configuration of fees for merchant accounts. These changes were deployed during a maintenance window, and the system was monitored for any adverse effects post-deployment.

short_description: Intermittent data loss in merchant review stage
description: Sales Agent encountered an error when trying to associate a new store location with an existing merchant ID, preventing the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic process. Initially, the Sales Agent reported an error when attempting to associate a new store location with an existing merchant ID during the onboarding process. The error occurred specifically during the e-signature stage, which is a critical step in the merchant onboarding workflow. The first step in the resolution was to replicate the issue in a controlled environment. The team used a staging environment that mirrored the production system to ensure accurate diagnostics. They started by checking the application logs for any relevant error messages. The logs indicated a '400 Bad Request' error when the e-signature module was invoked, which suggested a malformed request or a missing parameter. Using the application's logging framework, the team filtered logs by the merchant ID and the specific onboarding workflow to narrow down the issue. They then used the browser's developer tools to inspect the network requests and responses. The inspection revealed that the e-signature module was not receiving the required 'merchant_id' parameter in the POST request. This parameter was being omitted due to a bug in the front-end form validation logic. The front-end code was incorrectly checking for the presence of the 'merchant_id' field in the request body, but the backend API expected it to be included in the query parameters. This discrepancy caused the backend to reject the request with a '400 Bad Request' error. To resolve this, the development team implemented a fix in the front-end code to ensure the 'merchant_id' parameter was correctly included in the request body. They also updated the backend API to accept the parameter in both the request body and query parameters to ensure compatibility. Additionally, the team performed a code review to ensure that similar issues were not present in other parts of the application. The fix was then deployed to the staging environment, where it was thoroughly tested to ensure that the issue was resolved. Finally, the fix was rolled out to the production environment, and the Sales Agent was able to successfully complete the onboarding process without encountering the error.

short_description: PDF agreement not loading for Merchant
description: The dropdown menu for selecting equipment is not populating in the Sales UI, preventing Sales Agents from choosing the necessary devices for merchants.
resolution: The root cause of the issue was identified as restricted access permissions on the Sales Agent's account, which prevented the system from retrieving the Merchant Agreement PDF. To resolve this, the following steps were executed: 1. Checked the Sales Agent's role-based access control (RBAC) configuration in the CRM system to verify permissions for document retrieval. 2. Performed a detailed audit of the user's access rights using the 'audit_logs' command in the CRM's administrative console, which revealed missing permissions for accessing the 'MerchantAgreement' document type. 3. Updated the user's access rights by assigning the 'Document.Retrieve.MerchantAgreement' permission through the CRM's role management interface. 4. Verified the fix by re-testing the Sales UI, ensuring that the dropdown menu for equipment populated correctly and the PDF loaded without errors. Additionally, a temporary workaround was implemented to ensure that all Sales Agents with similar access issues would have their permissions automatically checked during login, preventing recurrence. The resolution was confirmed through multiple test cases and user acceptance testing (UAT) sessions.

short_description: PDF not loading for Merchant Agreement review
description: Sales Agent observes that the system is inaccurately calculating processing fees for a specific merchant account, leading to discrepancies in the final agreement.
resolution: Upon investigation, the root cause was identified as misconfigured fee parameters within the Payment Gateway integration module. The Sales Agent reported discrepancies in the processing fee calculations for merchant account 'M123456' during the review of a Merchant Agreement. Initial diagnostic steps included verifying the fee configuration settings in the backend system using the 'get_fee_parameters' API endpoint, which revealed an incorrect 'processing_fee_rate' value of 1.5% instead of the expected 2.2%. To resolve this, the IT Support team executed a script named 'reapply_fee_config.sh' that reinitialized the fee parameters for the affected merchant account. The script utilized the 'update_fee_parameters' API with the correct rate, and confirmed the change via a 'validate_fee_parameters' API call. Additionally, the team performed a database consistency check on the 'merchant_fee_config' table to ensure no residual incorrect entries remained. The resolution was verified by reprocessing the merchant agreement through the system's validation workflow, which confirmed the correct fee calculation. The incident was resolved without impacting other services, and the affected merchant account was monitored for 24 hours post-resolution to ensure stability.

short_description: Fee configuration tool malfunction in Sales UI
description: The Merchant reported that the PDF document for reviewing the agreement is not loading in the Customer UI, preventing them from proceeding with the onboarding process.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a multi-step diagnostic and remediation process. Initial troubleshooting began with verifying the user's browser compatibility and clearing browser cache and cookies, which did not resolve the issue. Next, we examined the Sales UI application logs and identified a 404 error when attempting to access the PDF document. This indicated a misconfiguration in the document storage path. Further investigation revealed that the 'ABC-2000' POS terminal model was not properly registered in the system database, causing the document retrieval service to fail. To resolve this, the database schema was updated to include the 'ABC-2000' model in the terminal_configuration table. Additionally, the document storage path was adjusted to reflect the new model's directory structure. We executed the following commands to update the database: 'UPDATE terminal_configuration SET is_active = TRUE WHERE model = 'ABC-2000';' and 'ALTER TABLE document_storage ADD COLUMN model VARCHAR(50);'. After the database update, we verified the changes using a SELECT query to confirm the model was correctly added. The document retrieval service was then restarted to ensure the new configuration was applied. Finally, we validated the fix by replicating the user's scenario and confirming the PDF document loaded successfully in the Customer UI.

short_description: Unable to add new location for merchant ID 12345
description: Sales Agent encountered an error while trying to onboard an additional location for an existing merchant ID. The system failed to save the new location details.
resolution: The incident was resolved through a systematic diagnostic approach. Initial troubleshooting indicated the issue was localized to the Sales UI interface. The first step was to verify if the problem was browser-specific by testing across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge). The Sales Agent was instructed to clear their browser cache and cookies, which are often the root cause of UI-related issues. After clearing the cache, the agent was also prompted to disable any browser extensions that might interfere with the UI's functionality. If the issue persisted, the next step was to perform a hard refresh of the browser by pressing Ctrl + F5 (Windows) or Cmd + Shift + R (Mac). Additionally, we checked for any pending updates or patches for the Sales UI application, ensuring it was running the latest stable version. To isolate the issue further, we executed a server-side diagnostic by checking the Sales UI server logs for any errors or exceptions related to the onboarding process. The logs revealed a potential session timeout issue where the user's session was being invalidated before the location details could be saved. To address this, we adjusted the session timeout configuration in the Sales UI server's configuration file (sales-ui-config.json), increasing the timeout from 30 minutes to 60 minutes. We also reviewed the authentication service logs to ensure there were no issues with token validation or session management. Finally, after implementing these changes, we performed a full restart of the Sales UI server to ensure all configurations were applied correctly. The Sales Agent was then able to successfully onboard the new location without any further interruptions.

short_description: Intermittent network connectivity affecting agreement review
description: Sales Agent noticed that any changes made to fees/services configurations for a merchant are not saving properly in the system.
resolution: The intermittent network connectivity issue affecting agreement review was diagnosed through a systematic approach.
