The engineer created a dedicated IoT SSID with Band Select disabled and 20MHz channel width. All 35 sensors associated cleanly and maintained 100% telemetry reporting.

short_description: Auditorium AP association limit reached during all-hands quarterly meeting
description: Over 80 attendees in the main auditorium were unable to connect to the Wi-Fi during the company-wide presentation, receiving 'Unable to join network'.
resolution: Checking client association counts on the auditorium APs via 'show ap active' revealed that both APs had hit their hardcoded maximum association limit of 200 clients each. The engineer temporarily increased the per-radio client limit from 200 to 400 ('config wlan max-associated-clients 400') and enabled load balancing across adjacent lobby APs. Queued devices connected immediately, distributing 420 active clients evenly across four radios.

short_description: Rogue AP containment misclassification disconnecting authorized guest hotspot
description: An executive presentation using an authorized cellular Verizon Wi-Fi backup puck kept dropping, with devices reporting constant deauthentication attacks.
resolution: Review of the Wireless Intrusion Prevention System (wIPS) logs showed that the WLC's Rogue AP Auto-Containment rule classified the cellular hotspot as a 'Malicious Rogue' broadcasting on the company's wired network and sent 802.11 deauthentication frames to disconnect it. The engineer marked the hotspot BSSID as 'Friendly / External' in the Rogue Management console and disabled automated wireless deauth containment for unverified rogues. Hotspot stability was restored immediately.

short_description: Wi-Fi 6 OFDMA feature incompatibility causing Intel laptop blue screens
description: Dozens of Dell laptops equipped with Intel AX201 Wi-Fi chipsets crashed with BSOD in Netwtw10.sys immediately upon associating to Wi-Fi 6 access points.
resolution: Analysis identified an interoperability bug between the AP firmware's 802.11ax Target Wake Time (TWT) / Downlink OFDMA and unpatched Intel wireless drivers. As an immediate workaround, the engineer temporarily disabled Downlink OFDMA on the 5GHz radio profile ('config wlan he downlink-ofdma disable 2'). Simultaneously, IT Support pushed updated Intel Wi-Fi driver v22.190 via Intune. Once drivers were updated, OFDMA was re-enabled with zero driver crashes.

short_description: RADIUS shared secret mismatch on newly deployed access point
description: Users connecting to access points on the 2nd floor expansion wing failed 802.1X authentication, with access points logging 'AAA server not responding'.
resolution: Diagnostics via 'test aaa-server radius' on the WLC passed, but per-AP FlexConnect local authentication failed. Inspection of the Network Access Device (NAD) entry in Cisco ISE revealed that the shared secret string configured for the 2nd-floor AP subnet had a missing character compared to the WLC profile. The engineer updated the RADIUS secret in ISE to match the global template and triggered an ISE policy sync. 802.1X authentications on the 2nd floor succeeded immediately.

short_description: FlexConnect local switching VLAN ACL blocking wireless printer discovery
description: Staff in regional branch offices connected to local Wi-Fi were unable to discover or print to local network printers via Bonjour / AirPrint.
resolution: Review of the branch FlexConnect group showed that an inbound FlexConnect ACL 'BRANCH-GUEST-ACL' was mistakenly mapped to the corporate internal VLAN 20. The ACL blocked multicast mDNS packets (UDP port 5353) required for AirPrint discovery. The engineer corrected the VLAN-to-ACL mapping under the FlexConnect group profile and added an explicit permit rule for mDNS UDP 5353. Local printer discovery succeeded immediately across all branch macOS and iOS devices.

short_description: Hidden node collision in logistics warehouse causing high packet retries
description: Forklift-mounted terminals in aisle 14 of the distribution center reported extreme input lag when scanning pallet barcodes, with retry counters reaching 48%.
resolution: A physical RF survey identified that tall metal racking blocked line-of-sight between terminals at opposite ends of the aisle, causing both to transmit simultaneously without carrier-sense detection (hidden node problem). The engineer lowered the RTS/CTS (Request to Send / Clear to Send) threshold from default 2347 bytes to 500 bytes on the warehouse 5GHz radio profile ('config wlan rts-threshold 500 3'). Collision-induced packet retries dropped from 48% to under 4%, eliminating scanner lag.

short_description: Wireless QoS profile misconfiguration mapping video to background queue
description: Executive board members experienced choppy video during an international video conference over the corporate Wi-Fi, while wired clients had flawless quality.
resolution: Inspecting the WLAN QoS settings via 'show wlan 1' showed the QoS profile set to 'Bronze' (Background - WMM AC_BK), which stripped DSCP markings from video streams and prioritized general web traffic over video. The engineer changed the QoS profile from Bronze to 'Platinum' (Voice & Video - WMM AC_VO) and enabled Fastlane DSCP marking trust. Wireless frame prioritization matched wired network QoS, resolving choppy video playback instantly.

short_description: BSSID beacon interval drift on outdoor mesh AP severing inter-building link
description: The wireless bridge connecting the main campus to the annex training facility dropped, isolating 40 employees in the annex from internal file shares.
resolution: Diagnostics on the outdoor mesh Root Access Point (RAP) showed the wireless bridge link to the Mesh Access Point (MAP) flapping every 90 seconds. A hardware clock drift caused beacon transmission intervals to desynchronize past the 100ms tolerance. The engineer updated the mesh profile with locked beacon intervals (100 TUs) and rebooted the RAP to sync hardware clocks with the central NTP server. The mesh backhaul link re-established and sustained 250Mbps throughput.

short_description: DHCP Option 43 missing on branch router preventing AP WLC discovery
description: Following replacement of a failed branch office router, four access points remained in an unconfigured state and failed to broadcast the corporate SSID.
resolution: Review of the newly provisioned branch DHCP server scope showed that DHCP Option 43 (vendor-specific option for WLC IP discovery) was omitted from the DHCP configuration. Without Option 43, lightweight APs could not locate the centralized controller across the WAN. The engineer added 'option 43 hex f104.0a0a.0a01' (pointing to controller IP 10.10.10.1) to the DHCP pool. The access points discovered the WLC on their next reboot, joined the cluster, and enabled all radios.

short_description: 802.1X session re-authentication timer set too low causing client lag
description: Engineering team reported micro-disconnects and brief SSH session stalls every 5 minutes while connected to the corporate wireless network.
resolution: Examination of the 802.1X advanced security profile on the WLC revealed 'Session Timeout' set to 300 seconds (5 minutes) with re-authentication enabled, forcing every client to execute a full 4-way handshake every 5 minutes. The engineer increased the 802.1X session timeout to 28800 seconds (8 hours) and enabled Fast SSID changing. Periodic re-authentication stalls ceased completely while maintaining daily security refresh cycles.

short_description: CleanAir spectrum analysis detecting cafeteria microwave oven interference
description: Laptops near the 1st-floor cafeteria experienced severe Wi-Fi slowdowns and packet loss every day between 12:00 PM and 1:30 PM.
resolution: Cisco CleanAir spectrum telemetry identified continuous non-Wi-Fi interference on channels 6 and 11, classified as 'Microwave Oven (Continuous Duty)' with a severity index of 92/100. Inspection revealed a damaged door seal on a high-wattage commercial cafeteria microwave emitting RF leakage. Facilities replaced the faulty microwave unit. CleanAir interference alarms cleared immediately, restoring 2.4GHz and 5GHz SNR above 32 dB.

short_description: PoE power budget exhaustion causing AP radio reboot under full load
description: Access point ap-fl2-east spontaneously rebooted whenever more than 25 clients connected simultaneously, dropping all users.
resolution: Checking switch port power telemetry via 'show power inline Gi1/0/12' showed the switch delivering legacy 802.3af power (15.4W). When client load increased, the dual-radio 4x4 Wi-Fi 6 AP exceeded the 15.4W threshold and triggered a brownout reboot. The switch stack power budget was constrained. The engineer reallocated PoE priority, enabled 802.3at PoE+ (30W) on the interface, and deployed a PoE+ injector. The AP drew 22.4W under peak load with zero reboots.

short_description: Guest wireless peer-to-peer client isolation failure exposing devices
description: Security audit reported that devices connected to the Visitor Guest Wi-Fi could discover and scan other visitors' laptops and tablets over the local subnet.
resolution: Review of the Guest WLAN configuration on the WLC confirmed that 'P2P Blocking Action' was set to 'Disabled', permitting peer-to-peer unicast and broadcast forwarding across the guest subnet. The engineer updated the WLAN policy with 'config wlan peer-blocking drop 3' to drop all inter-client traffic and enabled private-VLAN isolation on the underlying guest switchport. Re-testing confirmed total isolation between guest devices, with access restricted strictly to the internet gateway.

short_description: WLC High Availability redundancy link latency triggering false failover
description: The primary Wireless LAN Controller experienced a brief failover to the standby controller during core switch maintenance, causing 500 APs to re-negotiate CAPWAP sessions.
resolution: Diagnostics via 'show redundancy' showed the Redundancy Link (RP) between primary and standby controllers in HA stateful switchover (SSO) mode suffered keepalive packet loss due to optical attenuation on the dedicated fiber cross-connect. The engineer cleaned the optical transceiver connections, verified optical power at -12 dBm, and adjusted the keepalive retry count from 3 to 5 ('config redundancy keepalive-retries 5'). High Availability stabilized in ACTIVE/STANDBY-HOT state with 0 false failovers.

short_description: CoreDNS crash-looping in Kubernetes cluster due to recursive query loop
description: Production Kubernetes cluster prod-east-01 experienced widespread DNS resolution failures across all microservice pods, halting payment processing and order ingestion.
resolution: Inspecting pod logs via 'kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns' revealed fatal error 'plugin/loop: Loop (127.0.0.1:53 -> :53) detected'. A recent node resolv.conf update pointed upstream nameservers to local host IP (127.0.0.53), causing CoreDNS forwarding rules to recursively loop back onto itself until container memory exhausted. The engineer corrected the CoreDNS ConfigMap upstream forward block ('forward . 10.0.0.53 10.0.0.54') and restarted the CoreDNS deployment. Internal DNS queries resolved within 2ms, restoring cluster service communication.

short_description: Split-brain DNS zone transfer desync breaking payment gateway routing
description: Payment microservices reported intermittent host unreachable errors when calling internal gateway endpoint 'paygate.corp.internal', failing 50% of credit card transactions.
resolution: Executing 'dig @ns1.corp.internal paygate.corp.internal' returned active IP 10.20.4.50, but query against secondary server 'dig @ns2.corp.internal' returned obsolete decommissioned IP 10.20.4.12. Review of BIND logs identified AXFR zone transfer failure code 'REFUSED' due to an expired TSIG key on ns2. The engineer synchronized the HMAC-SHA256 TSIG secret across both nameservers and executed 'rndc retransfer corp.internal' on ns2. The zone updated to serial 2024030701, restoring consistent DNS responses across both resolvers.

short_description: DHCP relay IP helper address omission preventing client IP leasing
description: Workstations deployed on newly created engineering VLAN 75 received 169.254.x.x APIPA addresses, completely unable to communicate on the campus network.
resolution: Diagnostics on core switch sw-core-01 using 'show ip interface Vlan75' showed the Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) active, but 'Helper-address is not set'. Because DHCP requests are broadcast frames (255.255.255.255), routers dropped them at the Layer 3 boundary. The engineer added 'ip helper-address 10.10.1.15' and 'ip helper-address 10.10.1.16' (pointing to redundant Infoblox DHCP servers) under interface Vlan75. Workstations received valid DHCP lease configurations immediately.

short_description: NTP stratum clock drift causing Active Directory Kerberos auth failure
description: Hundreds of corporate users across multiple departments were locked out of Windows workstations and network file shares with error 'Kerberos authentication failed: Clock skew too great'.
resolution: Checking domain controller time telemetry via 'w32tm /query /status' revealed that the primary PDC Emulator clock had drifted 380 seconds ahead of international standard time, exceeding Kerberos's default 5-minute maximum tolerance. The upstream firewall had blocked NTP UDP port 123 during an automated security rule purge. The engineer restored outbound UDP 123 to pool.ntp.org, executed 'w32tm /resync /force' on the domain controllers, and propagated time sync across all campus switches and endpoints.

short_description: F5 BIG-IP VIP health monitor flapping on HTTP 301 permanent redirect
description: Internal CRM portal became intermittently unreachable; users experienced alternating successful page loads and 503 Service Unavailable errors.
resolution:
Review of the F5 BIG-IP Local Traffic Manager (LTM) pool logs revealed pool members marked 'Down (unchecked)' every 30 seconds. A recent web server patch enforced HTTPS redirection, responding with HTTP 301, while the F5 health monitor expected strictly 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK'. The engineer updated the monitor send string to 'GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: crm.corp.internal
Connection: Close

' and modified the receive string to '200|301|302'. Pool members stabilized in 'Available (Green)' state.

short_description: NGINX SSL reverse proxy SNI mismatch dropping multi-tenant connections
description: Customers visiting enterprise partner portal 'partner.company.com' received SSL handshake error 'SSL_ERROR_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME_ALERT' in their web browsers.
resolution: Inspection of NGINX reverse proxy error logs showed 'upstream SSL certificate verify failed' during client handshakes. The upstream backend cluster hosted multiple tenant domains, but the NGINX upstream proxy configuration was missing 'proxy_ssl_server_name on', failing to transmit Server Name Indication (SNI) to the backend. The engineer added 'proxy_ssl_server_name on' and 'proxy_ssl_name $host' to the location block, followed by 'nginx -s reload'. Handshakes completed cleanly with matching tenant SSL certificates.

short_description: Anycast DNS BGP route flapping causing high packet loss on recursive resolvers
description: External client DNS resolution experienced 35% packet drops and multi-second timeouts when querying company authoritative nameservers.
resolution: Diagnostics on the Anycast DNS edge routers showed that one node in Frankfurt had an unstable health-check script that repeatedly withdrew and announced the Anycast IP (198.51.100.53/32) into BGP every 45 seconds. BGP route dampening on global transit providers penalized the prefix. The engineer disabled the faulty node's ExaBGP daemon, resolved an out-of-memory issue in its local Unbound resolver process, and requested an upstream BGP unsuppress. Anycast routing stabilized with global query latency under 20ms.

short_description: Guest Wi-Fi DHCP pool exhaustion due to excessive 72-hour lease duration
description: Visitors attending a 2-day tech conference in the corporate auditorium could not acquire IP addresses on the guest network, with devices displaying 'No Internet Connection'.
resolution: Review of the Infoblox DHCP scope for Guest VLAN 150 (172.20.0.0/22 - 1,022 addresses) showed 100% utilization with 0 available leases. The default lease time was mistakenly configured for 72 hours (3 days), retaining stale leases for visitors who had already departed. The engineer reduced the DHCP lease duration to 4 hours ('lease 14400') and purged inactive offline leases older than 2 hours. Over 650 IP addresses were immediately returned to the pool, allowing attendees to connect.

short_description: BIND authoritative zone serial number rollback blocking secondary updates
description: Changes to internal DNS records for newly deployed microservices propagated to primary nameserver ns1, but secondary nameservers continued serving old IP addresses.
resolution: Inspection of zone files using 'named-checkzone' showed the primary zone serial was accidentally decremented from '2024032801' to '2024032701' by a configuration pipeline error. Because RFC 1982 dictates that secondary nameservers only update when the received serial is strictly higher, zone transfers were ignored. The engineer updated the zone serial to '2024032802' and issued 'rndc reload corp.internal' followed by 'rndc notify corp.internal'. Secondary servers updated immediately via IXFR.

short_description: F5 BIG-IP persistence cookie timeout causing e-commerce session drops
description: Customers shopping on the enterprise web store were randomly logged out and had their shopping carts emptied when navigating between checkout pages.
resolution: Traffic inspection revealed that the F5 BIG-IP cookie persistence profile was configured with an aggressive 60-second expiration instead of session-based persistence. If users took more than one minute to enter credit card details, their subsequent request hashed to a different backend server that lacked their local session cache. The engineer updated the cookie persistence profile to 'HTTP Cookie Insert' with expiration set to 3600 seconds and enabled cookie encryption. Shopping cart persistence was restored across checkout flows.

short_description: Infoblox Grid Master communication loss during WAN flap halting IPAM sync
description: Network automation scripts provisioning new server IP addresses failed with API timeout errors; regional DNS and DHCP appliances reported 'Grid Sync Offline'.
resolution: Diagnostics on the Infoblox Grid Master showed encrypted VPN communication tunnels to regional Grid members down following an MTU change on the core MPLS WAN. IPsec tunnel packets between grid members on UDP port 1194 were being dropped. The engineer enabled path MTU discovery on the WAN interface and restarted the Infoblox grid communication daemon ('set grid_conn_restart'). The grid synchronization restored to 'Online / Green', allowing automated IPAM provisioning to resume.

short_description: HAProxy frontend connection starvation from maxconn limit saturation
description: During a product launch marketing campaign, external users attempting to access the main website experienced HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors.
resolution: Checking HAProxy runtime statistics via 'echo "show info" | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.stat' showed 'CurrConns: 2000' and 'Maxconn: 2000' with a rapidly growing queue. The frontend reached its hardcoded maximum connection limit while backend servers were operating at only 25% CPU. The engineer increased 'maxconn 100000' in both global and frontend sections, tuned Linux kernel socket limits ('sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=65535'), and reloaded HAProxy smoothly ('systemctl reload haproxy'). Traffic unblocked immediately with zero dropped connections.

short_description: DNSSEC validation failure on corporate resolvers due to expired KSK
description: Employees were unable to access external corporate portal 'secure.example.com', with browsers returning 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN' on all internal workstations.
resolution: Running 'delv @10.0.0.53 secure.example.com' reported 'resolution failed: validation failure (expired RRSIG)'. The authoritative DNS registrar Key Signing Key (KSK) rollover had failed to update DS records at the parent TLD registrar, causing DNSSEC-validating internal resolvers to reject all responses as untrusted. The engineer submitted the new DS record hash (algorithm 13 - ECDSAP256SHA256) to the domain registrar and temporarily enabled DNSSEC permissive validation on the internal resolvers. Verification confirmed successful resolution.

short_description: Windows Server DHCP failover state out-of-sync causing duplicate IP assignments
description: Network monitoring alerted on widespread IP address conflict popups on employee laptops in Building C, resulting in disrupted network sessions.
resolution: Diagnostics on Windows Server DHCP failover cluster showed partner relationship state as 'Lost Contact'. While communication was broken, both primary and secondary servers entered independent lease assignment, issuing identical IP addresses to different workstations. The engineer restored firewall connectivity between the DHCP servers on TCP port 647, resolved the partner relationship state to 'Normal', and initiated an authoritative scope reconciliation ('Replicate Scope'). Duplicate IP alarms cleared.

short_description: Precision Time Protocol PTP clock drift in low-latency trading network
description: Financial trading execution algorithms alerted on timestamp discrepancy errors exceeding 50 microseconds across high-frequency execution nodes.
resolution: Telemetry on Arista low-latency switches showed PTP (IEEE 1588v2) Boundary Clock status in 'Uncalibrated' state. An optical GNSS satellite antenna connection had experienced water ingress, losing GPS lock and causing the Grandmaster Clock to enter holdover frequency drift. The engineer switched the active grandmaster source to the secondary atomic rubidium clock via PTP priority adjustment ('ptp priority1 127'). Clock offset returned to within 15 nanoseconds, satisfying strict regulatory time-stamping rules.

short_description: Azure Application Gateway 502 Bad Gateway from backend timeout mismatch
description: Users accessing public customer portals experienced intermittent HTTP 502 Bad Gateway responses during complex database reporting queries.
resolution: Analysis of Azure Application Gateway access logs showed error 'BackendConnectionTimeout'. The backend HTTP settings on the Application Gateway had a request timeout of 20 seconds, while backend reporting queries took up to 35 seconds to compute, causing the gateway to drop the TCP connection prematurely. The engineer increased the Application Gateway backend HTTP setting request timeout to 60 seconds and configured a dedicated health probe path ('/api/health') with 15-second intervals. 502 Bad Gateway errors dropped to zero.

short_description: DNS negative caching storing NXDOMAIN responses for newly provisioned hosts
description: Developers deploying new microservice 'billing-api.corp.internal' could not resolve the hostname for 2 hours after adding the DNS record, while public DNS worked.
resolution: Diagnostics showed developers had queried the hostname before the DNS record was created, causing recursive resolvers to cache the NXDOMAIN (Non-Existent Domain) negative response. The SOA record had an excessive Negative Caching TTL (MINIMUM field) set to 7200 seconds (2 hours). The engineer cleared the resolver cache via 'rndc flushname billing-api.corp.internal' and reduced the SOA negative caching TTL to 300 seconds. Resolvers queried the authoritative source and returned the correct IP immediately.

short_description: Redundant IP helper configuration causing DHCP broadcast packet storm
description: Datacenter core switches sw-core-01 and sw-core-02 reported high CPU utilization (90%) and buffer queue drops on management VLAN 10.
resolution: Packet capture on VLAN 10 showed millions of duplicated DHCP DISCOVER packets circulating between switches. Both core switches had mutual 'ip helper-address' pointing to each other across an active Layer 2 trunk, creating an endless DHCP broadcast forwarding loop. The engineer removed the circular helper statements, keeping helper addresses directed exclusively to the dedicated central DHCP server cluster (10.0.0.10, 10.0.0.11). CPU utilization on core switches returned to 8%.

short_description: F5 BIG-IP SSL cipher suite incompatibility dropping TLS 1.3 mobile apps
description: Mobile application users on iOS 17 and Android 14 reported connection failures when logging into the retail banking portal, with apps displaying network error.
resolution: SSL handshake inspection with 'openssl s_client -connect api.bank.com:443 -tls1_3' returned handshake failure alert 40. The F5 Client SSL profile was restricted to legacy TLS 1.2 RSA cipher suites, lacking support for modern elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman TLS 1.3 ciphers (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). The engineer updated the Client SSL profile to enable TLS 1.3, enabled ECDSA certificates alongside RSA, and applied cipher group 'DEFAULT:!3DES:!RC4'. Mobile application logins succeeded instantly.

short_description: AWS Route 53 Resolver outbound security group blocking hybrid DNS
description: Workloads in AWS cloud VPCs were unable to resolve on-premises corporate domain names (*.corp.internal), halting hybrid cloud database queries.
resolution: CloudWatch logs for the Route 53 Outbound Resolver Endpoints showed query timeouts to on-premises DNS IPs. Review of the Amazon VPC security group attached to the resolver network interfaces revealed that egress rule for UDP/TCP port 53 had been deleted during a terraform cleanup. The engineer added an egress rule permitting UDP and TCP port 53 to the corporate on-premises DNS subnet (10.0.0.0/16). Route 53 outbound queries succeeded, restoring hybrid domain resolution.

short_description: CoreDNS cache plugin memory leak causing pod OOMKilled evictions
description: Kubernetes cluster experienced cyclic DNS degradation every 4 hours as CoreDNS pods were continuously terminated by the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory killer.
resolution: Prometheus container memory metrics showed CoreDNS memory climbing continuously to the 256Mi limit. A high volume of unique negative DNS queries from dynamic CI/CD containers overwhelmed the CoreDNS cache plugin without item eviction. The engineer tuned the CoreDNS ConfigMap cache settings to enforce a 30-second maximum TTL on negative responses ('denial 9984 30') and raised the container memory limit to 512Mi. Memory stabilized at 110Mi, eliminating pod evictions.

short_description: Load balancer source IP hash affinity overloading single backend node
description: Web server node web-03 crashed under 99% CPU load while neighboring web-01 and web-02 were operating at only 5% utilization.
resolution: Load balancer telemetry showed that all incoming requests originated from a regional corporate web proxy that NATted 5,000 users behind a single public IP address. Because the load balancer was configured with 'Source IP Hash' persistence, every single user request was mapped to the exact same backend server. The engineer changed the load balancing algorithm from Source IP Hash to 'Round Robin with Cookie Persistence'. Traffic distributed evenly across all three backend nodes within minutes.

short_description: Microsoft CA CRL distribution point DNS lookup failure blocking SSL
description: Internal HTTPS servers and VPN endpoints rejected user client certificates with error 'The revocation status of the certificate could not be determined'.
resolution: Executing 'certutil -verify -urlfetch client_cert.cer' showed that certificate validation stalled while attempting to fetch the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) from 'crl.corp.internal/pki/corp.crl'. The DNS record for the internal web server hosting the CRL had been deleted during zone cleanup. The engineer recreated the DNS A record pointing to 10.10.2.20 and confirmed HTTP accessibility via curl. Client certificate revocation checks succeeded immediately across all network gateways.

short_description: Dynamic DNS TSIG key authentication failure preventing PTR record updates
description: Linux servers obtaining DHCP leases failed to register reverse DNS PTR records in the Windows DNS zone, causing reverse IP lookups to fail for automated log analysis.
resolution: ISC DHCP server logs showed error 'Unable to add reverse map: NOTAUTH'. The Transaction Signature (TSIG) key used by the DHCP daemon to authenticate Dynamic DNS (DDNS) updates to Windows Server DNS had expired and was out of sync. The engineer generated a new HMAC-MD5 TSIG key, imported it into both Windows DNS security settings and dhcpd.conf ('key dhcp-dns-key { algorithm hmac-md5; secret ...; }'), and restarted dhcpd. Reverse PTR records registered automatically upon next lease renewal.

short_description: F5 BIG-IP LTM SNAT pool port exhaustion during batch API data upload
description: Batch invoice processing jobs failed midway through nightly sync, with application servers reporting 'Cannot assign requested address' when calling external payment APIs.
resolution: Checking F5 LTM statistics via 'tmsh show ltm snatpool SNAT-OUTBOUND' showed all 65,535 ephemeral source ports in use across the configured SNAT IP. The batch job opened tens of thousands of rapid, short-lived HTTP connections that lingered in TIME_WAIT state, exhausting the single IP's port space. The engineer expanded the SNAT pool by adding three additional egress IP addresses ('tmsh modify ltm snatpool SNAT-OUTBOUND members add { 198.51.100.11 198.51.100.12 198.51.100.13 }') and enabled TCP port reuse. Batch API uploads succeeded without port exhaustion.

short_description: AWS Direct Connect Private VIF BGP down from customer ASN mismatch
description: The dedicated 10Gbps AWS Direct Connect link to the primary production VPC failed to establish BGP peering, forcing all cloud database traffic across high-latency IPsec backup tunnels.
resolution: Diagnostics on edge router rtr-dx-01 via 'show ip bgp summary' showed neighbor 169.254.248.1 stuck in Idle state. Inspection of the AWS Direct Connect Virtual Interface (VIF) configuration showed AWS expected Customer ASN 64512, whereas the router's local BGP process was configured with legacy ASN 65000. The engineer updated the BGP peer configuration to 'neighbor 169.254.248.1 local-as 64512' and verified MD5 authentication key. BGP peering transitioned to Established within 10 seconds, restoring 10Gbps low-latency Direct Connect routing.

short_description: Azure ExpressRoute BFD session drop causing asymmetric circuit failover
description: Production database replication to Azure East US region experienced sudden 25% packet drops and out-of-order packet delivery during normal operational hours.
resolution: Telemetry on edge router rtr-er-01 revealed that Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on ExpressRoute Primary circuit tore down due to intermittent optical frame errors from the telco provider. Outbound traffic failed over to the Secondary circuit while inbound Azure traffic continued returning on the Primary circuit, creating an asymmetric routing state across stateful firewalls. The engineer tuned BFD timers on the Primary link ('bfd interval 300 min_rx 300 multiplier 5') and forced symmetric traffic via BGP local preference until telco fiber was cleaned.

short_description: VXLAN EVPN Type-2 MAC/IP route sync failure from missing route-target import
description: Newly provisioned compute nodes on Leaf-04 were unable to communicate with existing virtual machines on Leaf-01 across data center fabric VLAN 200.
resolution: Running 'show bgp l2vpn evpn' on Leaf-04 showed that EVPN Type-2 (MAC/IP advertisement) routes from Leaf-01 were received in BGP but not installed into the EVPN mac-table. The Virtual Network Identifier (VNI 10200) configuration on Leaf-04 had a typo in the route-target import statement ('route-target import 65001:10201' instead of '10200'). The engineer corrected the route-target import statement under VRF EVPN configuration. Type-2 routes immediately installed, restoring cross-leaf East-West communication.

short_description: Spine-leaf underlay MTU mismatch causing VXLAN encapsulated packet drops
description: Large database queries and file syncs between datacenter clusters timed out, while standard ping and small HTTP transactions succeeded.
resolution: Packet trace on the spine switch interconnects revealed that VXLAN encapsulation adds 50 bytes of overhead (Outer Ethernet, IP, UDP, and VXLAN headers). When host VMs transmitted standard 1500-byte packets, encapsulated frames reached 1550 bytes. Intermediate underlay spine links were configured with standard MTU 1500 rather than jumbo frames, dropping the packets silently. The engineer enabled jumbo MTU 9216 across all physical spine-leaf underlay interfaces and port-channels. Large payload transfers completed with 0% packet loss.

short_description: BGP unnumbered peering failure over IPv6 link-local on bare-metal host
description: High-performance computing bare-metal worker node hpc-node-12 failed to establish dynamic routing with Top-of-Rack switch tor-sw-01, leaving compute jobs unscheduled.
resolution: Diagnostics on tor-sw-01 using 'show bgp ipv4 unicast summary' showed the BGP unnumbered neighbor over interface Eth1/12 stuck in Active state. Linux FRRouting logs on the host showed IPv6 router advertisements (RA) disabled on interface enp3s0f0, preventing IPv6 link-local neighbor discovery required for RFC 5549 BGP unnumbered peering. The engineer enabled IPv6 forwarding and router advertisements on the server ('sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.enp3s0f0.accept_ra=2'). BGP unnumbered established immediately, advertising the host's /32 Loopback IP.

short_description: AWS Transit Gateway route propagation omission dropping inter-VPC traffic
description: Microservices in the Payments VPC were unable to reach authentication microservices in the Core-Services VPC following an automated Terraform infrastructure deployment.
resolution: Analysis of the AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) route tables showed that while the Payments VPC attachment existed, 'Route Propagation' was disabled on the TGW default route table for the new VPC. Consequently, the Payments subnet CIDR (10.150.0.0/16) was absent from the routing table. The engineer enabled route propagation for the Payments VPC attachment via AWS CLI ('aws ec2 enable-transit-gateway-route-table-propagation'). Routes propagated instantly across the TGW mesh, restoring inter-VPC connectivity.

short_description: Azure Virtual WAN hub route map stripping required BGP communities
description: Branch offices connected to Azure Virtual WAN (vWAN) were routing regional SaaS traffic through expensive European hubs instead of local US breakouts.
resolution: BGP route analysis on the branch edge router showed that custom regional BGP community tags (65515:100) were missing from prefixes advertised by Azure Virtual WAN. A newly applied vWAN hub route map was configured to re-tag routes but omitted 'additive', effectively replacing existing communities with the default Azure ASN. The engineer updated the Azure vWAN route map policy to preserve incoming BGP communities. Local breakout path selection normalized across all branch routers.

short_description: VTEP NVE loopback reachability loss causing VXLAN overlay tunnel collapse
description: All Layer 2 and Layer 3 overlay traffic terminated on leaf switch Leaf-02 dropped completely, isolating an entire server rack.
resolution: Checking 'show nve peers' on neighboring leaves showed Leaf-02 in 'Down' state. On Leaf-02, 'show interface nve 1' showed the Network Virtualization Endpoint (NVE) down because its source loopback interface (Loopback 1 - 10.255.1.2) was unadvertised in the OSPF underlay following a configuration commit error. The engineer added 'ip ospf 1 area 0' to interface Loopback 1. Spines relearned the VTEP IP, NVE 1 re-established peer sessions, and all VXLAN overlay VNIs recovered.

short_description: ECMP hash polarization saturating single 100GbE spine uplink
description: Spine-01 uplink interface Eth1/1 was congested at 98Gbps with continuous buffer queue drops, while parallel uplinks Eth1/2, Eth1/3, and Eth1/4 hovered at only 12Gbps.
resolution: Diagnostics confirmed ECMP hash polarization: traffic traversing two successive layers of switches used identical CRC-32 5-tuple hash polynomials, causing traffic hashed to link 1 on the top-of-rack switch to consistently hash to link 1 on the spine. The engineer configured a unique hash polynomial seed on all spine switches using 'load-sharing hash-seed 42890' and enabled inner VXLAN packet header inspection for hashing. Traffic distributed evenly across all four 100GbE links (approx 34Gbps each).

short_description: MLAG peer-link heartbeat loss causing dual-active split-brain loop
description: Datacenter leaf switch pair sw-leaf-01A and sw-leaf-01B experienced a temporary split-brain state, corrupting MAC forwarding tables and dropping VM traffic.
resolution: Syslog showed '%MLAG-3-PEER_DOWN: Peer link down, heartbeat failed'. An engineer had accidentally disabled the dedicated out-of-band management VLAN carrying the backup peer-keepalive heartbeat while the physical peer-link was undergoing transceiver replacement. Both switches assumed the primary active role. The engineer restored the backup heartbeat interface, enabled dual-active detection, and brought the peer-link back up. MLAG negotiated cleanly to Active/Standby roles, resolving the forwarding loop.

short_description: AWS Direct Connect Gateway route table limit exceeded dropping subnets
description: Newly provisioned on-premises datacenter subnets (10.210.0.0/16) were unreachable from any AWS VPC, with AWS cloud servers returning Destination Host Unreachable.
resolution: AWS Personal Health Dashboard flagged an alert: 'Direct Connect Gateway route limit reached (100 prefixes)'. On-premises border routers were advertising individual /24 subnets instead of summarized supernets, hitting AWS's hard limit of 100 advertised routes per DXGW. Any prefix beyond 100 was silently discarded. The engineer configured BGP route summarization on the edge routers, consolidating 85 individual routes into 4 summarized /16 CIDRs. AWS DXGW accepted all prefixes, restoring complete hybrid cloud reachability.

short_description: VXLAN EVPN Type-5 route missing default gateway IP blocking WAN breakout
description: Virtual machines in datacenter VRF 'Production-App' could communicate internally, but all outbound internet traffic to external cloud APIs timed out.
resolution: Inspection via 'show bgp l2vpn evpn route-type 5' on border leaf switches showed the 0.0.0.0/0 default route being advertised without an encapsulation gateway IP (GW-IP) attribute. Compute leaf switches were unable to resolve the next-hop VTEP for external traffic. The engineer configured 'advertise l2vpn evpn' under the VRF routing instance with 'default-originate' and explicit border leaf router MAC binding. Compute leaves installed the Type-5 default route into their forwarding tables, restoring external internet egress.

short_description: Google Cloud Interconnect VLAN attachment BGP stuck in Active state
description: The dedicated 10Gbps Partner Interconnect to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) failed to come online during scheduled data migration, stalling multi-terabyte data transfers.
resolution: Checking 'show ip bgp neighbors 169.254.10.1' on edge router rtr-gcp-01 showed zero BGP messages received. Investigation of the Google Cloud Cloud Router configuration revealed an MD5 authentication string mismatch: GCP had BGP MD5 authentication enabled, while the local on-premises router sub-interface lacked the 'neighbor password' command. The engineer configured matching BGP MD5 credentials on rtr-gcp-01. The BGP session immediately transitioned to Established, establishing GCP interconnect routing.

short_description: Anycast Gateway Distributed L3 routing MAC conflict across EVPN fabric
description: Hosts in VLAN 100 experienced intermittent gateway reachability drops and IP address conflict warnings, with ping latency fluctuating between 1ms and 450ms.
resolution: In VXLAN EVPN Symmetric IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging), all leaf switches acting as Anycast Gateways for a VNI must share an identical virtual MAC address. Review showed Leaf-03 was configured with virtual MAC '0000.5e00.0101' while Leaf-01 and Leaf-02 had '0000.5e00.0102'. This discrepancy caused hosts to continuously thrash their ARP caches as they roamed between racks. The engineer standardized the anycast gateway MAC across all switches via 'fabric forwarding anycast-gateway-mac 0000.5e00.0101'. Gateway reachability stabilized.

short_description: Data Center Interconnect EVPN Multisite border gateway desync
description: Disaster recovery failover test between Ashburn and Phoenix datacenters failed; virtual machines in Ashburn could not ping their replicated counterparts in Phoenix.
resolution: Diagnostics on the EVPN Multisite Border Gateway (BGW) routers showed that BGP EVPN Type-4 Ethernet Segment routes were being filtered by the provider WAN edge. Without Type-4 routes, the border gateways could not discover remote VTEPs or establish multi-site overlay tunnels. The engineer enabled 'l2vpn evpn' address family peering across the dedicated inter-datacenter dark-fiber link and disabled WAN route-filtering for EVPN attributes. Border gateways established BGW-to-BGW tunnels, restoring cross-site replication.

short_description: RoCEv2 Priority Flow Control deadlock stalling AI GPU cluster training
description: A distributed large language model training job spanning 64 NVIDIA H100 GPUs stalled completely, with switches reporting input buffer saturation and zero throughput.
resolution: Inspection of Arista leaf switch buffer counters identified a Priority Flow Control (PFC) deadlock on traffic class 3 (lossless RoCEv2). When a brief transient congestion loop formed, PFC pause frames propagated cyclically across the spine-leaf fabric in an endless pause loop. The engineer enabled Dynamic PFC Deadlock Watchdog ('priority-flow-control watchdog enable' with 100ms detection and recovery) and tuned Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) marking thresholds. The watchdog automatically broke the pause loop, restoring line-rate GPU training.

short_description: AWS VPC peering connection dropping 9001-byte jumbo frames between EC2 instances
description: High-speed data ingestion pipelines running on EC2 instances experienced severe throughput drops (falling from 25Gbps to 800Mbps) when transferring datasets across an inter-region VPC peering link.
resolution: Packet trace on the Linux instances using 'tracepath' showed path MTU discovery failing at 1500 bytes. While intra-VPC traffic supports 9001-byte jumbo frames, AWS inter-region VPC peering strictly enforces an MTU of 1500 bytes. The application instances had interface MTU set to 9001 without Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) enabled, resulting in silent packet drops. The engineer applied TCP MSS clamping ('iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu') on the instances. Throughput restored immediately.

short_description: Azure ExpressRoute Microsoft Peering NAT IP exhaustion blocking M365
description: Corporate headquarters employees were unable to access Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, or SharePoint, while general public internet browsing operated normally.
resolution: Diagnostics on the border firewall routing ExpressRoute Microsoft Peering showed NAT pool exhaustion. Microsoft Peering requires dedicated public IP NAT for corporate users accessing M365 endpoints over the ExpressRoute circuit. The NAT pool of four /30 IP addresses exhausted its 240,000 translation sessions under heavy Teams video conferencing. The engineer assigned a dedicated /27 public IP block to the Microsoft Peering NAT pool and configured port block allocation. M365 services reconnected immediately.

short_description: Leaf switch TCAM profile misallocation preventing VXLAN ACL compilation
description: A security micro-segmentation update failed to deploy to spine-leaf switch sw-leaf-08, with the network automation engine reporting 'Hardware programming error'.
resolution: Checking switch logs via 'show hardware internal tcam allocation' revealed that the switch was using the default Enterprise TCAM profile, which allocated 80% of TCAM space to Layer 2 MAC tables and only 5% to VXLAN VTEP/ACL lookups. The newly injected security policy exceeded available ACL slices. The engineer reconfigured the switch TCAM profile to 'vxlan-routing' mode via 'hardware profile tcam vxlan-routing' and scheduled a reload during the maintenance window. ACL programming succeeded cleanly.

short_description: BGP Add-Path capability disabled on Route Reflector causing EVPN path suppression
description: Multi-homed compute servers dual-connected to separate leaf switches experienced 50% packet drop due to unannounced redundant next-hops.
resolution: Analysis on the spine BGP Route Reflectors (RR) revealed that when two leaf switches advertised identical EVPN routes for an Active-Active multihomed host, the RR only reflected its single best-path, hiding the second path from other leaves. BGP Add-Path capability was disabled. The engineer configured 'neighbor SPINE-PEERS capability additional-paths send receive' and 'bgp additional-paths select all' on the route reflectors. Leaves received both ECMP paths, enabling true active-active load sharing across leaves.

short_description: AWS Transit Gateway multicast domain failure stopping market data feed
description: Algorithmic trading engines in AWS VPCs stopped receiving real-time stock ticker multicast data feeds originating from on-premises financial exchanges.
resolution: Inspection of the AWS Transit Gateway Multicast Domain configuration showed that while the multicast group (239.255.10.1) was defined, the subnet network interfaces of the newly scaled EC2 trading instances were not registered as Multicast Group Members. The engineer updated the infrastructure automation script to automatically register instance ENIs using 'aws ec2 register-transit-gateway-multicast-group-members'. Multicast traffic flowed into the instances within seconds.

short_description: EVPN ARP suppression cache timeout causing excessive overlay broadcast flood
description: Datacenter leaf switch uplinks experienced high broadcast bandwidth consumption, with packet counters showing millions of ARP requests flooded across the VXLAN fabric.
resolution: Review of the EVPN fabric configuration showed that ARP Suppression was disabled on several newly provisioned VNIs. Without local ARP suppression, leaf switches were forced to flood host ARP broadcast packets as BUM (Broadcast, Unknown Unicast, Multicast) traffic to all VTEPs in the overlay. The engineer enabled 'suppress-arp' under each VNI configuration ('nve vni 10100 suppress-arp') across all leaf switches. Leaf switches responded to ARP requests locally from their EVPN host tables, reducing fabric broadcast traffic by 94%.

short_description: Azure Route Server BGP route limit exceeded dropping dynamic NVA routes
description: Network Virtual Appliances (NVAs) in Azure Hub failed to inject updated inspection routes, resulting in uninspected traffic bypassing corporate security policies.
resolution: Azure Network Watcher diagnostics showed that the Azure Route Server (ARS) had exceeded its hard limit of 1,000 dynamic BGP routes learned from the third-party firewall appliances. ARS stopped accepting subsequent route advertisements. The engineer configured route-filtering on the NVAs to withdraw granular /28 branch subnets and advertise summarized regional /16 CIDRs instead, reducing total advertised routes to 42. ARS re-synchronized and successfully propagated routing to all spoke VPCs.

short_description: ECN WRED marking failure causing micro-burst buffer drops in spine switches
description: Distributed storage cluster Ceph reported high latency write operations and osd timeouts despite network links showing less than 40% average utilization.
resolution: Buffer monitoring on Cisco Nexus 9000 spine switches identified egress queue tail-drops during bursty storage writes. Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) with Weighted Random Early Detection (WRED) was configured, but the minimum threshold was set too high (15MB), allowing the switch shared buffer to overflow before ECN Congestion Experienced (CE) bits were marked on IP headers. The engineer lowered the WRED minimum threshold to 2MB and maximum threshold to 6MB. Storage endpoints throttled back early upon seeing CE bits, eliminating buffer drops.

short_description: Cisco Nexus vPC orphan port flapping during secondary switch reboot
description: Single-homed database server db-standby-01 disconnected for 8 minutes during a rolling software upgrade of redundant datacenter switches.
resolution: Investigation revealed that db-standby-01 was connected to a single switch (an orphan port on vPC secondary switch sw-leaf-02) rather than dual-homed. When the vPC peer-link failed during switch reload, the vPC orphan port suspended feature was not configured, causing the switch to drop the server's traffic. The engineer migrated the database server to an active-active dual-homed LACP port-channel across both vPC peers and configured 'vpc orphan-port suspend' on remaining single-homed ports. Server connectivity remained continuous during subsequent reloads.

short_description: YubiKey 5 NFC FIDO2 PIN locked after failed attempts blocking Okta SSO
description: Senior financial auditor was locked out of corporate Okta SSO portal after three incorrect FIDO2 PIN entries on their YubiKey 5 NFC hardware token.
resolution: IT Support connected the user's hardware token via YubiKey Manager CLI ('ykman fido info') which confirmed 'PIN is blocked (0 attempts remaining)'. Because FIDO2 security architecture enforces hardware lockout to prevent brute-force attacks, the FIDO2 application required a physical reset. The technician issued 'ykman fido reset', re-registered the user's hardware key in Okta Admin Console under Multi-Factor Authentication > FIDO2 (WebAuthn), and guided the user to configure a new 8-digit PIN. The user authenticated into Okta successfully.

short_description: Entra Conditional Access blocking remote login due to Intune compliance lag
description: A field sales executive was blocked from accessing Microsoft 365 apps on their company Dell laptop, receiving error 'You cannot get there from here'.
resolution: Review of Microsoft Entra sign-in logs identified Conditional Access Policy 'CAP-ENFORCE-COMPLIANT-DEVICE' failure with status 'Device not in compliant state'. The Intune management portal showed the laptop in 'Pending evaluation' because the Windows Defender antivirus signature definition had not refreshed over slow cellular Wi-Fi. The technician triggered a manual Intune sync via Windows Settings > Accounts > Access Work or School > Info > Sync and ran 'mpcmdrun.exe -SignatureUpdate'. Intune compliance evaluated to Compliant within 5 minutes, clearing the Conditional Access block.

short_description: Okta FastPass biometric verification failure following macOS Sequoia update
description: Developers upgrading to macOS Sequoia reported that Okta FastPass failed with error 'Biometrics verification was cancelled or timed out', forcing SMS fallback.
resolution: Diagnostics revealed that the macOS major OS upgrade revoked Okta Verify's access to the Secure Enclave LocalAuthentication API. The technician opened macOS Terminal and ran 'tccutil reset All com.okta.mobile' to clear corrupt privacy permissions, uninstalled the outdated client, and deployed Okta Verify v9.22 via Jamf Pro. Upon re-launch, Okta Verify prompted for Touch ID authorization. FastPass passwordless verification completed seamlessly.

short_description: PIV smartcard middleware driver conflict freezing Windows logon screen
description: Government contracts team workstations froze on a black screen with a spinning circle whenever an employee inserted their PIV smartcard into the USB reader.
resolution: Event Viewer logs under System flagged 'Winlogon warning: Smart Card Resource Manager failed to read ATR'. A recent Windows Update installed an incompatible generic CCID smartcard driver that conflicted with ActivClient 7.4 middleware. The technician booted the machines in Safe Mode, rolled back the USB CCID driver via Device Manager to the certified Identiv driver, and rebuilt the local smartcard certificate cache using 'certutil -scinfo'. Smartcard PIN authentication and Windows logon resumed without freezing.

short_description: WebAuthn attestation mismatch in Chrome preventing passwordless login
description: Engineers using Google Chrome on Ubuntu workstations were unable to authenticate into internal GitLab using FIDO2 keys, receiving 'WebAuthn: Invalid attestation'.
resolution: Inspection of browser developer console logs showed that Chrome 122 enforced WebAuthn Enterprise Attestation, while the GitLab authentication backend only accepted 'direct' or 'none' attestation. The technician updated GitLab's omniauth configuration in gitlab.rb to include 'attestation: direct' and added udev rules ('/etc/udev/rules.d/70-u2f.rules') granting non-root user access to hidraw USB devices. GitLab reconfigured cleanly, and developers logged in via FIDO2 keys without errors.

short_description: Duo Mobile MFA push notification failure from APNs token de-registration
description: Executives traveling internationally stopped receiving Duo push notifications on their iPhones, requiring manual 6-digit passcode entry for every login.
resolution: Duo Admin logs showed status 'Push notification dropped: APNs registration expired' following an iOS iCloud device migration. Apple Push Notification service (APNs) had invalidated the device token. In Duo Admin Panel, the technician navigated to Users > Selected User > Phones, sent an SMS activation link to re-link the Duo Mobile account, and guided the user to tap 'Reconnect Account'. Test push succeeded immediately, restoring one-tap MFA approvals.

short_description: Active Directory account lockout loop from stale Windows Credential Manager
description: Marketing Director's Active Directory account locked out every 15 minutes automatically, even after IT Support reset the password multiple times.
resolution: Domain controller security audit logs (Event ID 4740) showed caller computer name as the user's desktop workstation. Investigation identified an old mapped network drive script and Microsoft Outlook storing an expired password in Windows Credential Manager under 'Windows Credentials > Generic Credentials'. The technician unlocked the account via Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC), navigated to Credential Manager, deleted the stale cached entries, and re-authenticated Outlook with the current password. Account lockouts ceased completely.

short_description: Kerberos TGS decryption error 0x1f following service account password reset
description: Internal business intelligence reports failed across the company with error 'Kerberos authentication failed: KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED (0x1f)'.
resolution: Event Viewer on the SQL reporting server showed Event ID 40960 ('The security system detected an authentication error: Target Name SQLSvc/db-bi.corp.internal'). The service account password had been rotated, but the IIS Application Pool identity cached the old Kerberos ticket encryption key. The technician purged stale tickets using 'klist purge' on the application servers, restarted the IIS application pool ('iisreset /restart'), and verified the Service Principal Name (SPN) with 'setspn -L SQLSvc'. Reports generated successfully without Kerberos errors.

short_description: Windows Hello for Business enrollment failure 0x801c044f from missing TPM EK
description: Employees receiving newly imaged Lenovo ThinkPad laptops were unable to set up PIN or facial recognition, receiving error code 0x801c044f.
resolution: Diagnostics via 'dsregcmd /status' showed 'NgcSet : NO' and TPM attestation failure. Inspection of the TPM chip revealed that the OEM Endorsement Key (EK) certificate was not pre-installed in the firmware. The technician updated the laptop UEFI BIOS to version 1.45, cleared the TPM via 'tpm.msc', and ran 'CertReq -enroll -q' to provision a cloud-managed Microsoft attestation certificate. Windows Hello for Business setup completed successfully, allowing biometric PIN creation.

short_description: SAML 2.0 signature verification failure on Salesforce from expired IdP cert
description: Entire sales organization was locked out of Salesforce CRM, receiving error 'Single Sign-On Error: We can't log you in because of an issue with SAML verification'.
resolution: Okta System Logs flagged 'SAML assertion validation error: IdP certificate expired'. The Okta SAML application signing certificate for Salesforce had expired at midnight. In Okta Admin, the technician generated a new self-signed X.509 signing certificate, downloaded the metadata XML, and uploaded the public certificate into Salesforce Single Sign-On Settings under 'Identity Provider Certificate'. A test SAML login confirmed successful assertion validation, restoring access for 280 sales reps.

short_description: Entra PIM role activation blocked by MFA authentication strength mismatch
description: Cloud DevOps engineers were unable to activate privileged 'Global Administrator' roles in Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM), receiving 'MFA requirement not met'.
resolution: Review of the Entra PIM policy showed that role activation recently enforced 'Phishing-resistant MFA' authentication strength. The engineers had authenticated using SMS OTP and Microsoft Authenticator push notifications, which do not satisfy phishing-resistant criteria. The technician assisted the engineers in registering their enterprise YubiKey 5 NFC hardware keys under My Sign-Ins > Security Info. Upon re-authenticating with FIDO2 hardware keys, PIM role activations succeeded instantly.

short_description: YubiKey PIV certificate slot 9a expired blocking federal portal access
description: Compliance officers were rejected when accessing government compliance portals with error 'Client certificate has expired or is invalid'.
resolution: Using YubiKey Manager ('ykman piv info'), the technician inspected PIV Slot 9a (Authentication) and confirmed the user certificate expired the previous day. The technician used the enterprise PKI enrollment agent portal to issue a renewed 2-year X.509 client certificate, imported the certificate and private key to Slot 9a via 'ykman piv certificates import 9a user_cert.pfx', and cleared the local certificate propagation service. The user authenticated into the federal compliance portal immediately.

short_description: Okta Verify TOTP clock drift desynchronizing 6-digit passcode validation
description: An executive traveling across time zones was unable to log into corporate apps using Okta 6-digit TOTP codes, receiving 'Invalid code' on every attempt.
resolution: Investigation revealed that the executive had manually set their smartphone clock 3 minutes behind actual time while in flight, exceeding the standard RFC 6238 60-second time-step window. The technician guided the user to iOS Settings > General > Date & Time and toggled 'Set Automatically' to ON, resynchronizing with Apple NTP servers. The subsequent 6-digit code was validated successfully by Okta.

short_description: SCIM user provisioning synchronization failure between Entra ID and Slack
description: Thirty new employees hired this week were unable to join Slack Enterprise Grid; accounts were missing from the Slack workspace despite being active in HR systems.
resolution: Checking Entra ID Enterprise Applications > Slack > Provisioning Logs showed error 'HTTP 401 Unauthorized: SCIM token expired'. The OAuth bearer secret token used by Entra ID to communicate with Slack SCIM API had expired after 180 days. The technician regenerated the SCIM API token in Slack Admin Console, updated the Secret Token field in Entra ID Provisioning Settings, and triggered 'Restart provisioning'. All 30 accounts provisioned into Slack with correct channel assignments.

short_description: Azure AD Kerberos ticket issuance failure for cloud-joined laptop SMB access
description: Remote engineers on Entra-joined Windows 11 laptops were prompted for network credentials when accessing on-premises file shares (\\files.corp.internal\shares).
resolution: Diagnostics on a client machine using 'klist' showed no Kerberos tickets for 'cifs/files.corp.internal'. Inspection in Entra ID revealed that the Azure AD Kerberos Server object in the on-premises domain had a stale krbtgt decryption key following a forest recovery. The technician executed 'Set-AzureADKerberosServer' in PowerShell to rotate the Cloud Kerberos keys and synchronized the domain with Entra Connect. Cloud-joined laptops acquired valid Kerberos TGTs and accessed file shares seamlessly.

short_description: FIDO2 security key registration rejected due to restricted AAGUID policy
description: Employees purchasing Feitian FIDO2 keys could not register them as security keys in the Microsoft My Sign-Ins portal, receiving 'Security key model not permitted'.
resolution: Review of Entra ID Authentication Methods > FIDO2 Security Keys configuration showed 'Enforce attestation' enabled with an explicit allow-list of Authenticator Attestation GUIDs (AAGUIDs) restricted strictly to Yubico keys. The technician added the Feitian ePass FIDO2 AAGUID (1811a2f6-3d44-42b7-8494-0f2c7a72d733) to the approved hardware security key list in Entra Admin Center. Employees registered their Feitian keys successfully.

short_description: LDAP bind authentication timeout on legacy internal wiki server
description: Internal technical documentation wiki displayed 'Error 500: LDAP Server Unreachable' preventing employees from searching standard operating procedures.
resolution: Diagnostics on the wiki Linux server using 'ldapsearch -x -H ldaps://dc01.corp.internal:636' showed connection timed out. Domain controller dc01 had been decommissioned during active directory consolidation, but the wiki's LocalSettings.php had hardcoded dc01's IP address. The technician updated the configuration to point to the generic DNS round-robin record 'ldaps://corp.internal:636' and added internal root CA certificate to '/etc/ssl/certs'. LDAP binds completed in 12ms, restoring wiki access.

short_description: Microsoft Authenticator number matching prompt missing on Apple Watch
description: Users reported that Microsoft Authenticator notifications on their Apple Watch failed to display the 2-digit number matching prompt, causing sign-in timeouts.
resolution: Investigation confirmed an architecture limitation: Apple Watch companion app for Microsoft Authenticator does not support the cryptographic number matching required by Microsoft Entra's modern security baselines. The technician issued an IT knowledge base bulletin informing users to approve prompts directly on their iPhone lock screens and updated Intune MAM app protection policies to ensure notifications display full number-matching interactive dialogues on iOS.

short_description: OAuth 2.0 refresh token expiration forcing daily Outlook re-authentication
description: Executive assistants reported having to enter passwords and MFA prompts every morning in Microsoft Outlook desktop client, disrupting workflow.
resolution: Analysis of sign-in telemetry showed Conditional Access policy 'Session Controls > Sign-in Frequency' was set to 12 hours, forcing OAuth 2.0 Primary Refresh Token (PRT) invalidation overnight. The technician updated the Conditional Access session lifetime policy for compliant enterprise devices to 14 days with Persistent Browser Session enabled. Daily re-authentication prompts ceased, maintaining secure biometric sign-on via Windows Hello.

short_description: YubiKey Smart Card Minidriver missing blocking certificate PIN prompt
description: Engineers plugging in YubiKeys on fresh Windows 11 installs were not prompted for a PIN when signing Git commits with GPG/PIV, failing code reviews.
resolution: Device Manager showed 'YubiKey 5' under Other Devices with a yellow warning triangle. The Windows 11 base image lacked the proprietary Yubico Smart Card Minidriver required for Windows Base Cryptographic Service Provider (CSP) integration. The technician deployed the YubiKey Minidriver MSI via Intune and restarted the smartcard service ('net stop scardsvr && net start scardsvr'). The PIN prompt appeared immediately upon commit signing.

short_description: PingFederate Single Log-Out redirect loop caused by corrupted browser cookie
description: Users logging out of enterprise expense portal were trapped in an infinite HTTP 302 redirect loop between the app and PingFederate IdP.
resolution: Browser network trace showed SAML Single Logout (SLO) endpoint repeatedly failing to clear the encrypted 'PF' tracking cookie due to a SameSite attribute mismatch. The technician cleared the client browser cache and updated the PingFederate server configuration ('run.properties') to enforce 'pf.cookie.samesite=Lax' across all IdP-initiated logout endpoints. The logout redirect loop resolved, cleanly terminating SSO sessions.

short_description: Active Directory replication lag delaying security group access rights
description: An employee promoted to database administrator could not access production SQL servers despite IT Support adding them to the DBA security group two hours earlier.
resolution: Checking replication topology via 'repadmin /showrepl' revealed that the domain controller in the employee's branch office had not replicated with the primary DC due to an RPC communication pause. The technician ran 'repadmin /syncall /AeD' to force immediate inter-site directory synchronization and had the user execute 'klist purge' on their desktop to renew their Kerberos group membership tokens. The employee accessed the database servers immediately.

short_description: Touch ID sudo authentication bypassed by PAM syntax error on macOS
description: Security compliance scanning flagged that developer MacBooks failed Touch ID enforcement for elevated sudo operations in Terminal.
resolution: Inspection of '/etc/pam.d/sudo' showed the pam_tid.so line was placed below standard pam_smartcard.so and pam_opendirectory.so modules, causing PAM evaluation to skip biometric verification. The technician deployed a corrected PAM configuration script via Jamf Pro that inserted 'auth sufficient pam_tid.so' at line 1 of '/etc/pam.d/sudo' and set file immutability flags. Touch ID prompt appeared on subsequent sudo invocations.

short_description: Entra ID Passwordless phone sign-in failure with error code 50074
description: Staff attempting passwordless phone sign-in through Microsoft Authenticator were denied access with error code 50074 (User did not pass MFA challenge).
resolution: Entra ID sign-in diagnostics indicated that the user's Microsoft Authenticator app had lost device registration with the Entra tenant after the user restored their phone from a backup. The technician had the user log into My Sign-Ins with a Temporary Access Pass (TAP), remove the broken authenticator entry, and re-register Microsoft Authenticator with 'Enable phone sign-in' selected. Passwordless authentication resumed seamlessly.

short_description: Smart card PIN change failure through Windows Security dialog due to blocked PUK
description: Executive assistant attempting to change their smart card PIN received error 'The PIN could not be changed: The PIN Unblocking Key (PUK) is blocked'.
resolution: Checking smart card status using 'certutil -scinfo' confirmed that the card's PUK retry counter was exhausted (0 tries remaining) from repeated incorrect administrator attempts. The technician used the enterprise Smart Card Management System (SCMS) administrative console to perform an authenticated challenge-response administrative unblock, reset the PUK retry counter to 5, and set a new compliant 8-digit PIN. The user verified smartcard logon to their workstation.

short_description: Windows Print Spooler crashing in spoolsv.exe from corrupt Type 3 driver
description: Finance department workstations were unable to print invoices; the Windows Print Spooler service stopped spontaneously every 30 seconds across 15 laptops.
resolution: Application Event Viewer logs showed Event ID 1000 with faulting module 'hpz3r5zp.dll' in 'spoolsv.exe'. An outdated legacy Type 3 printer driver deployed via GPO was corrupting the print spooler memory buffer. The technician stopped the Print Spooler service ('net stop spooler'), cleared stuck spool files from 'C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\', deleted the offending driver files from 'spool\drivers\x64', and deployed the updated Microsoft certified Type 4 V4 Universal Print Driver. The spooler service started cleanly and all queued invoices printed without crashes.

short_description: Windows Search indexing high CPU freezing File Explorer on laptop
description: A financial analyst reported their laptop was completely unresponsive, with fans running at maximum speed and File Explorer freezing whenever opening folders.
resolution: Task Manager showed 'SearchIndexer.exe' consuming 98% CPU and 4GB RAM. The Windows Search catalog database ('Windows.edb') had expanded to 85GB due to indexing an unexcluded local git repository containing millions of small source code files. The technician stopped 'WSearch', deleted the bloated database at 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Search\Data\Applications\Windows\Windows.edb', rebuilt the index via Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild, and excluded '.git' and 'node_modules' directories. CPU utilization dropped to 2%.

short_description: macOS launchd crash loop from orphaned security agent daemon plist
description: Developer MacBook Pros exhibited extreme battery drain and thermal throttling, with the macOS Console showing thousands of error messages per minute.
resolution: Inspection of system logs via 'log show --predicate 'process == "launchd"' --last 5m' revealed launchd repeatedly spawning a non-existent binary '/usr/local/bin/legacy_dlp_agent' every 10 seconds with exit code 127. An uninstalled DLP security product had left an orphaned plist in '/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.vendor.dlp.plist'. The technician unloaded and deleted the stale launch daemon using 'sudo launchctl bootout system/com.vendor.dlp' and 'sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.vendor.dlp.plist'. Crash loop stopped and CPU idle restored to 95%.

short_description: BitLocker recovery key prompt on every reboot following UEFI BIOS update
description: Engineering manager was prompted to enter a 48-digit BitLocker recovery key every time their Dell Precision workstation booted up or restarted.
resolution: Diagnostics via 'manage-bde -status C:' confirmed BitLocker was locked in recovery mode. A recent automated Dell SupportAssist BIOS update altered the TPM 2.0 Platform Configuration Registers (PCR 0 and PCR 2), causing TPM seal validation to fail during boot. The technician suspended BitLocker protection for one reboot via 'manage-bde -protectors -disable C:', rebooted into Windows, and re-bound the TPM measurements using 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:'. The system resumed normal passwordless TPM boot.

short_description: Thunderbolt 4 dock dual monitor flickering from outdated DisplayLink driver
description: Executives in Building A experienced continuous black-screen flickering every 45 seconds on their dual 4K external monitors connected via USB-C docking stations.
resolution: Hardware diagnostics identified that the Lenovo ThinkPad Universal Thunderbolt 4 docks were running outdated DisplayLink USB graphics driver v10.1, which had a known memory leak bug when driving dual 60Hz 4K displays over USB-C alternate mode. The technician deployed the certified DisplayLink v11.4 M2 driver package and updated the dock firmware via the Lenovo Dock Manager utility. Dual monitor display stabilized with zero screen flickering.

short_description: Windows 11 BSOD DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL in rtwlan6.sys on sleep wake
description: HP ProBook laptops across the sales department crashed with a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) whenever users opened their laptop lids after sleep mode.
resolution: Kernel memory dump analysis using WinDbg ('!analyze -v') pointed to stop code `0x000000D1 (DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL)` with faulting symbol `rtwlan6.sys` (Realtek 8822CE Wireless LAN driver). The driver failed power state transition from D3cold to D0. The technician uninstalled the legacy OEM driver and pushed the updated Microsoft WHQL driver v2024.10.138 via Intune Windows Update rings. Sleep wake testing confirmed 0 crashes across 50 consecutive wake cycles.

short_description: Realtek Audio driver conflict causing microphone muting during Teams calls
description: Employees reported their laptop microphones randomly muted midway through client Teams presentations, showing 'Your microphone isn't working'.
resolution: Inspection in Device Manager showed an audio enhancement driver conflict between Realtek High Definition Audio and Waves MaxxAudio Service. A background Waves audio processing crash was seizing the microphone exclusive mode handle. The technician opened Sound Settings > Microphone Properties > Advanced, unchecked 'Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device', and disabled MaxxAudio APO processing in the registry. Microphone audio stream remained stable throughout hour-long Teams calls.

short_description: WinSxS Component Store corruption blocking mandatory Windows security updates
description: Monthly cumulative security updates failed to install on executive laptops, reverting changes at 96% with error code 0x800f0922.
resolution: Review of 'C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log' revealed manifest corruption in the Windows Component Store (WinSxS). The technician executed Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM) with health repair ('DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth') pulling clean files from Windows Update, followed by System File Checker ('sfc /scannow') which repaired corrupted system DLLs. Upon reboot, the cumulative security update installed cleanly without rollback.

short_description: macOS System Integrity Protection blocking legacy kernel extension
description: Video production team's Mac Studio could not mount high-speed Promise RAID external storage enclosures following a macOS Sonoma update.
resolution: System logs showed 'Kext rejected: System Integrity Protection prevented loading of com.promise.driver.stex'. Apple has deprecated legacy Kernel Extensions (KEXTs) in favor of modern DriverKit System Extensions. The technician verified the storage vendor had released a certified DriverKit system extension. The technician downloaded and installed the DriverKit package, approved the system extension under macOS System Settings > Privacy & Security, and restarted the Mac. The Promise RAID volumes mounted at full 2800MB/s speed.

short_description: Windows User Profile Service failed logon assigning temporary TEMP profile
description: Senior accountant logged into their desktop and found all desktop icons, browser bookmarks, and mapped files missing, with Windows notifying 'You have been signed in with a temporary profile'.
resolution: Registry inspection under 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList' showed the user's SID key appended with '.bak', indicating that an ungraceful shutdown locked 'NTUSER.DAT'. The technician had the user sign out, signed in with local admin, deleted the temporary profile key without .bak, removed the '.bak' suffix from the original SID entry, and verified 'State' was set to 0. Upon user logon, the original user profile loaded properly with all desktop files and personal preferences intact.

short_description: 100% disk usage from Windows SysMain service thrashing workstation storage
description: Warehouse inventory management terminals were experiencing multi-minute delays opening inventory software, with Task Manager reporting 100% continuous disk utilization.
resolution: Resource Monitor identified 'SysMain' (formerly SuperFetch) executing continuous high-volume read/write operations against prefetch files on the SATA storage drives. On older solid-state and mechanical drives, aggressive memory page preloading causes severe I/O bottlenecking. The technician stopped and disabled the SysMain service ('sc config SysMain start=disabled && sc stop SysMain') via elevated command prompt and cleared 'C:\Windows\Prefetch'. Disk utilization immediately dropped from 100% to 4%, restoring application response times.

short_description: USB-C power delivery negotiation failure cycling external monitor off
description: Dell Latitude laptops connected to Dell UltraSharp USB-C monitors suffered from the monitor blacking out and reconnecting every 3 minutes.
resolution: Diagnostics showed the monitor attempted to deliver 90W Power Delivery (PD) over a substandard 60W-rated USB-C cable that had been swapped by a user. When the laptop engaged high performance mode, current draw exceeded the cable's e-marker chip specification, triggering the monitor's over-current protection reset. The technician replaced the generic cable with an active 100W 40Gbps Thunderbolt certified cable. Power delivery negotiated stably at 90W and monitor cycling ceased.

short_description: WSL2 virtual switch network virtualization failure following Hyper-V update
description: Software engineers reported that Ubuntu containers inside Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 lost internet and LAN connectivity, reporting 'Network is unreachable'.
resolution: Diagnostics in PowerShell via 'Get-VMSwitch' showed the internal Hyper-V Virtual Switch 'WSL' in a corrupted disconnected state following a Windows 11 feature update. The technician shut down all WSL instances ('wsl --shutdown'), reset the Windows network stack ('netsh int ip reset' and 'netsh winsock reset'), and configured WSL2 to use modern Mirrored Networking mode by creating '%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig' with '[wsl2]\nnetworkingMode=mirrored'. WSL2 booted with native host network sharing, restoring full container reachability.

short_description: macOS Keychain Access password prompt loop after Active Directory password change
description: An employee changing their corporate password received dozens of popups stating 'macOS wants to use the "login" keychain. Please enter the keychain password'.
resolution: Because the user updated their enterprise Active Directory password via web portal while disconnected from the corporate network, the local macOS 'login' keychain remained encrypted with their old password. The technician launched Keychain Access, selected Settings > 'Update Keychain Password', entered the old password followed by the new corporate password, and synchronized the keychain master key. The popup cascade resolved immediately.

short_description: Windows time drift causing Outlook calendar meetings to display wrong hour
description: Human Resources team reported that scheduled interviews in Outlook calendar were appearing one hour earlier than scheduled across five recruiter laptops.
